extraction_notes.note: Artefact of the missing \end{proof}: Lemma D.8 sits inside the proof environment of Lemma D.5 and so counts as part of it; the proof of Theorem 5.1 uses Lemma D.8, while the proof of Lemma D.5 genuinely uses Theorem 5.1. No circular argument in the paper itself.

The proof of Lemma D.5 has no \end{proof}, so its proof environment runs to the end of Appendix D and contains Lemmas D.6-D.9, subsections D.3-D.4 and the proofs of Theorems 5.1 and 5.2. The environment span is kept; the embedded blocks are setup steps of it and are nested inside it.
Proofs are identified by '(of \cref{...})' in the body rather than an optional argument; the proof following Property D.9 is the proof of Theorem 5.1, so its proves edge was set by hand.
The informal Lemmas 1.1 and 1.2 in the introduction restate Theorem 3.1 and Lemma 4.3; treated as repeated statements (also_stated_at) rather than separate lemma nodes.
Numbered equation (2) is called 'the classic descent lemma for SGD'; typed lemma (external, uncited) rather than equation.
The proof of Theorem 5.2 is a whole appendix subsection in prose (D.4) without its own proof environment; emitted as a prose proof node.
The sentence 'where Sigma_{v_t} := sum_i v_{t,i}.' after Lemma D.5 completes that lemma but lies outside its environment; no separate node (the proof restates the definition).

nodes.name: AdaGrad-Norm
nodes.statement:
This paper investigates the norm version of AdaGrad (known as AdaGrad-Norm), which is a single stepsize adaptation method and is formally described as  egin{equation}  egin{aligned} S_{n}=S_{n-1}+ ig\|
abla g(	heta_{n},\xi_{n}) ig\|^{2}, \quad 	heta_{n+1}=	heta_{n}- rac{\alpha_0}{\sqrt{S_{n}}}
abla g(	heta_{n},\xi_{n}), \end{aligned}\end{equation} where $S_{0}$ and $\alpha_{0}$ are pre-determined positive constants, and the stochastic gradient $
abla g(	heta_{n},\xi_{n})$ is an estimation of the true gradient $
abla g(	heta_n)$ with the noise variable $\xi_n$.
nodes.origin_citation: Duchi et al. 2011 (AdaGrad); Ward et al. 2020 (AdaGrad-Norm)
nodes.statement_short: AdaGrad-Norm: accumulate squared stochastic-gradient norms in $S_n$ and step with size $\alpha_0/\sqrt{S_n}$.

nodes.name: AdaGrad-Norm update rule
nodes.statement: \begin{aligned} S_{n}=S_{n-1}+\big\|\nabla g(\theta_{n},\xi_{n})\big\|^{2}, \quad \theta_{n+1}=\theta_{n}-\frac{\alpha_0}{\sqrt{S_{n}}}\nabla g(\theta_{n},\xi_{n}), \end{aligned}
nodes.label: AdaGrad_Norm

nodes.name: Accumulate squared gradient norm
nodes.statement: S_{n}=S_{n-1}+\big\|\nabla g(\theta_{n},\xi_{n})\big\|^{2},
nodes.statement_short: Add the squared stochastic-gradient norm to the accumulator $S_n$

nodes.name: Adaptive gradient step
nodes.statement: \theta_{n+1}=\theta_{n}-\frac{\alpha_0}{\sqrt{S_{n}}}\nabla g(\theta_{n},\xi_{n}),
nodes.statement_short: Move against the stochastic gradient with step size $\alpha_0/\sqrt{S_n}$

nodes.name: Almost sure convergence
nodes.statement: Almost sure convergence, defined as $\lim_{n \rightarrow \infty} \left\|\nabla g(\theta_n) \right\|=0 \ \ a.s.$, provides a robust guarantee that the algorithm will converge to the critical point with probability 1 during a single run of the stochastic method.

nodes.name: Descent lemma for SGD
nodes.statement: \mathbb{E}[g(\theta_{n+1}) \mid \mathscr{F}_{n-1}] - g(\theta_{n})\le -\alpha_{n}\|\nabla g(\theta_{n})\|^{2}+\frac{ L\alpha_{n}^{2}}{2}\mathbb{E}\left[\|\nabla g(\theta_{n},\xi_{n})\|^{2} \mid \mathscr{F}_{n-1}\right].
nodes.statement_short: One-step expected decrease of $g$ for SGD under $L$-smoothness, with a quadratic step-size error term.
nodes.label: descent:sgd

nodes.name: Mean-square convergence
nodes.statement: In addition to almost sure convergence, mean-square convergence (MSE) is another critical criterion, formulated by $\lim_{n \rightarrow \infty} \mathbb{E}\left\|\nabla g(\theta_{n}) \right\|^2 = 0$.

nodes.name: Indicator function
nodes.statement: We use $\mathbb{I}_{X}(x) = 1 $ if $x \in X$ and $\mathbb{I}_{X}(x) = 0$ otherwise to denote the indicator function.

nodes.name: Critical points set and critical value set
nodes.statement: We define the critical points set $\Theta^{\ast}:=\{\theta \mid \nabla g(\theta)=0\}$ and the critical value set $g(\Theta^{\ast}):=\{g(\theta) \mid \nabla g(\theta)=0\}$.

nodes.name: Expectation and conditional expectation notation
nodes.statement: We use $\mathbb{E}[\cdot]$ denote the expectation on the probability space and $\mathbb{E}[\cdot \mid \mathscr{F}_{n}]$ denote the conditional expectation on the $\sigma$-field $\mathscr{F}_{n}$.

nodes.name: Notation for squared expectation
nodes.statement: For notational convenience, $\mathbb{E}[X^2]$ denotes the expectation on the square of the random variable $X$ and $\mathbb{E}^2[X]$ represents the square of the expectation on the random variable $X$.

nodes.name: Reversed-summation convention
nodes.statement: To make the notation $\sum_{a}^{b}(\cdot)$ consistent, we let $\sum_{a}^{b}(\cdot) \equiv -\sum_{b}^{a}(\cdot)\ (\forall\ b< a).$
also_stated_at: If the upper index of the summation is less than the lower index, we define the summation to be zero, i.e., $\sum_{s}^{t}(\cdot) \equiv -\sum_{t}^{s}(\cdot)\ (\forall\ t<s)$.

nodes.name: Index set [d]
nodes.statement: The notation $[d]$ denotes the set of the integers $\left\lbrace 1,2,\cdots, d\right\rbrace$.

nodes.name: Unconstrained non-convex optimization problem
nodes.statement: Throughout the sequel, we consider the unconstrained non-convex optimization problem \begin{align} \min_{\theta \in \mathbb{R}^d} \,\, g(\theta), \end{align} where $g: \mathbb{R}^d \rightarrow \mathbb{R}$ satisfies the following assumptions.
nodes.statement_short: Minimize a smooth, possibly non-convex $g$ over $\mathbb{R}^d$.

nodes.name: Optimization problem P1
nodes.statement: \min_{\theta \in \mathbb{R}^d} \,\, g(\theta),
nodes.label: P1

nodes.name: Assumption on the objective function
nodes.statement:
The objective function $g(	heta)$ satisfies the following conditions:  egin{enumerate}[label=	extnormal{(oman*)},leftmargin=*] \item $g(	heta)$ is continuously differentiable and non-negative. \item $
abla g(	heta)$ is Lipschitz continuous, i.e., $  ig\|
abla g(	heta)-
abla g(	heta') ig\|\le L\|	heta-	heta'\| $, for all $	heta, 	heta' \in \mathbb{R}^{d}$. \item(	extbf{Only for asymptotic convergence}) $g(	heta)$ is not asymptotically flat, i.e., there exists $\eta>0$ such that $\liminf_{\|	heta\|ightarrow+\infty} \|
abla g(	heta)\|^{2}>\eta.$ \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: $g$ is $C^1$, non-negative, $L$-smooth, and (for asymptotics) not asymptotically flat.
nodes.label: ass_g_poi

nodes.name: Stochastic first-order oracle (SFO)
nodes.statement: This paper focuses on the stochastic methods through a stochastic first-order oracle (SFO) which takes an input $\theta_n \in \mathbb{R}^d$ and returns a random vector $\nabla g(\theta_n, \xi_n)$ drawn from the probability space $(\Omega, \left\lbrace\mathscr{F}_n \right\rbrace_{n\ge 1}, \mathbb{P})$.

nodes.name: Independent noise sequence
nodes.statement: The noise sequence $\{\xi_{n}\}$ consists of independent random variables.

nodes.name: Natural filtration
nodes.statement: We denote the $\sigma$-filtration $\mathscr{F}_{n}:=\sigma\{\theta_{1},\xi_{1},\xi_{2},...,\xi_{n}\}$ for $n\geq 1$, with $\mathscr{F}_{i}:=\{\emptyset,\ \Omega\}$ for $i=0$, and define $\mathscr{F}_{\infty}:=\bigcup_{n=1}^{+\infty}\mathscr{F}_{n}$.

nodes.name: Assumption on the stochastic gradient (affine noise variance)
nodes.statement:
The stochastic gradient $
abla g(	heta_n, \xi_n)$ satisfies  egin{enumerate}[label=	extnormal{(oman*)},leftmargin=*] \item $\mathbb{E} \left[
abla g(	heta_n, \xi_n) \mid \mathscr{F}_{n-1}ight] = 
abla g(	heta_n)$. \item (	extbf{Affine noise variance}) $\mathbb{E}\left[ ig\|
abla g(	heta_n,\xi_{n}) ig\|^{2} \mid \mathscr{F}_{n-1}ight]\le \sigma_{0} ig\|
abla g(	heta_n) ig\|^{2}+\sigma_{1}$, for some constants $\sigma_{0}, \sigma_{1} \geq 0$. \item(	extbf{Only for asymptotic convergence}) For any $	heta_n$ satisfying $\|
abla g(	heta_{n})\|^{2}<D_0$, it holds that $\|
abla g(	heta_{n},\xi_{n})\|^{2}< D_1$ a.s.. for some constants $D_0, D_1 >0$. \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: Unbiased stochastic gradients with affine noise variance, and bounded noise near critical points (asymptotics only).
nodes.label: ass_noise

nodes.name: Mini-batch model satisfies the bounded-noise condition
nodes.statement: Under~\cref{ass_g_poi}, the widely used mini-batch stochastic gradient model satisfies~\cref{ass_noise:i3} of \cref{ass_noise}. Since the near-critical case at infinity is excluded (\cref{ass_g_poi}~\ref{ass_g_poi:i3}), we can identify a sufficiently small $D_0$ such that the near-critical points set $\{\theta \mid \|\nabla g(\theta)\|<D_0\}$ remains bounded. Consequently, when the stochastic gradient is Lipschitz continuous, the mini-batch stochastic gradients will remain within a bounded set, thereby satisfying \cref{ass_noise:i3}.
nodes.statement_short: Mini-batch stochastic gradients satisfy Assumption 2.2(iii) because near-critical sets are bounded.

nodes.name: Descent inequality for AdaGrad-Norm
nodes.label: inequ:smooth:inequality

nodes.name: Decomposition of the descent inequality
nodes.label: inequ:sufficient:decrease

nodes.name: Difference of inverse square roots of S_n
nodes.statement: \frac{1}{\sqrt{S_{n-1}}} - \frac{1}{\sqrt{S_{n}}} = \frac{\|\nabla g(\theta_{n},\xi_{n})\|^{2}}{\sqrt{S_{n-1}}\sqrt{S_{n}}\cdot(\sqrt{S_{n-1}}+\sqrt{S_{n}})}.
nodes.label: inequ:sn:minus:sn1

nodes.name: Notations zeta, R, Lambda, Gamma and martingale X_n
nodes.statement: In this decomposition, we define the martingale sequence $X_{n}$ and introduce the notations $\zeta(n), R_n, \Lambda_n, \Gamma_n$ to simplify the expression given in \cref{inequ:sufficient:decrease}.
nodes.statement_short: Names the terms of the decomposition (5): martingale $X_n$ and $\zeta(n),R_n,\Lambda_n,\Gamma_n$.

nodes.name: Lyapunov function g-hat and MDS X-hat
nodes.statement: Furthermore, we introduce $\hat{g}(\theta_n)$ as the Lyapunov function and $\{ \hat{X}_n, \mathscr{F}_{n}\}_{n\ge 1}$ is a new martingale difference sequence (MDS) to achieve the key sufficient decrease inequality as follows.

nodes.name: Sufficient decrease inequality
nodes.statement: ({\bf Sufficient decrease inequality}) Under \cref{ass_g_poi}~\ref{ass_g_poi:i}$\sim$\ref{ass_g_poi:i2} and \cref{ass_noise}~\ref{ass_noise:i}$\sim$ \ref{ass_noise:i2}, consider the sequence $\{\theta_{n}\}$ generated by AdaGrad-Norm, we have \begin{align} \hat{g}(\theta_{n+1}) - \hat{g}(\theta_n) \leq -\frac{\alpha_{0}}{4}\zeta(n)+C_{\Gamma, 1}\cdot \Gamma_n + C_{\Gamma, 2}\frac{\Gamma_n}{\sqrt{S_{n}}} + \alpha_0 \hat{X}_{n}, \end{align} where $\hat{g}(\theta_{n}):=g(\theta_{n})+ \frac{\sigma_{0}\alpha_{0}}{2}\zeta(n)$, $\hat{X}_n = X_n + V_n$, and $V_n$ is defined in \cref{notation:Vn}. The constant terms $C_{\Gamma, 1}, C_{\Gamma, 2}$ are defined in \cref{notation:ghat:const}.
assumptions: consider the sequence $\{\theta_{n}\}$ generated by AdaGrad-Norm
nodes.statement_short: Lyapunov function $\hat g$ decreases by $\tfrac{\alpha_0}{4}\zeta(n)$ up to summable $\Gamma_n$ terms and a martingale difference.
nodes.label: sufficient:lem

nodes.name: Sufficient decrease inequality (display)
nodes.statement: \hat{g}(\theta_{n+1}) - \hat{g}(\theta_n) \leq -\frac{\alpha_{0}}{4}\zeta(n)+C_{\Gamma, 1}\cdot \Gamma_n + C_{\Gamma, 2}\frac{\Gamma_n}{\sqrt{S_{n}}} + \alpha_0 \hat{X}_{n},

nodes.name: Stability of AdaGrad-Norm
nodes.statement: If \cref{ass_g_poi,ass_noise} hold, then for AdaGrad-Norm there exists a sufficiently large constant $\tilde{M}>0,$ such that \begin{equation}\nonumber\begin{aligned} \mathbb{E}\Big[\sup_{n\ge 1}g(\theta_{n})\Big]< \tilde{M}<+\infty, \end{aligned}\end{equation} where $\tilde{M}$ depends on the initial state of the algorithm and the constants in assumptions.
conclusions: for AdaGrad-Norm there exists a sufficiently large constant $\tilde{M}>0,$ such that
also_stated_at: (Informal) Consider AdaGrad-Norm under appropriate conditions, there exists a constant $\tilde{M} > 0$ such that \begin{equation}\nonumber \mathbb{E}\Big[\sup_{n \ge 1}g(\theta_{n})\Big] < \tilde{M} < +\infty. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: The expected supremum of the loss along AdaGrad-Norm iterates is finite.
nodes.label: stable

nodes.name: Almost-sure boundedness of the loss from stability
nodes.statement: From \cref{stable}, we can conclude that for any given trajectory, the value of the function remains bounded (\(\sup_{n \ge 1} g(\theta_{n}) < +\infty \)) almost surely. Note that the boundedness of the expected supremum function value $\mathbb{E}[\sup_{n \ge 1} g(\theta_n)] < \infty$ is a stronger form of stability than the almost-sure boundedness of the supremum alone, i.e., $\sup_{n \ge 1} g(\theta_n) < +\infty$ a.s. The latter condition is insufficient to ensure mean-square convergence.
nodes.statement_short: Stability gives $\sup_n g(\theta_n)<\infty$ a.s.; the expected-supremum bound is strictly stronger.

oindent{ f Phase I:} To demonstrate the stability of the loss function sequence \(\{g(	heta_{n})\}_{n\ge 1}\), the key technique is to segment the entire iteration process according to the value of the Lyapunov function \(\hat{g}(	heta_{n})\). Specifically, we define the non-decreasing stopping times $\{	au_{t}\}_{t\ge 1}$ as  egin{align} &	au_{1}:=\min\{k\ge 1:\hat{g}(	heta_{k})>\Delta_0\},\ 	au_{2}:=\min\{k\ge 	au_{1}: \hat{g}(	heta_{k})\le \Delta_0\ 	ext{or}\ \hat{g}(	heta_{k})>2\Delta_0\},
otag\&	au_{3}:=\min\{k\ge 	au_{2}:\hat{g}(	heta_{k})\le \Delta_0\},..., 
otag\&	au_{3i-2}:=\min\{k> 	au_{3i-3}:\hat{g}(	heta_{k})>\Delta_0\},\ 
otag \ &	au_{3i-1}:=\min\{k\ge 	au_{3i-2}:\hat{g}(	heta_{k})\le \Delta_0\ 	ext{or}\ \hat{g}(	heta_{k})>2\Delta_0\},
otag\&	au_{3i}:=\min\{k\ge 	au_{3i-1}:\hat{g}(	heta_{k})\le \Delta_0\}. \end{align} where $\Delta_0:=\max\{C_{0},\hat{C}_{g}\}$ and $C_0, \hat{C}_g$ are defined in \cref{lem:adj:ghat} and \cref{pro_0}, respectively. {For the first three stopping time $	au_1, 	au_2, 	au_3$, we have $	au_1 \leq 	au_2 \leq 	au_3$. When $	au_1 = 	au_2$, we have $\hat{g}(	heta_{	au_1}) > 2 \Delta_0$ while we have $	au_2 < 	au_3$ such that $\hat{g}(	heta_{	au_3}) \leq \Delta_0$ and $\hat{g}(	heta_n) > \Delta_0$ for $n \in [	au_1, 	au_3)$. If $	au_1 < 	au_2$ (that is $\Delta_0 < \hat{g}(	heta_{	au_1}) < 2\Delta_0$), no matter $	au_2 = 	au_3$ or $	au_2 < 	au_3$, we have $\hat{g}(	heta_n) > \Delta_0$ for any $n \in [	au_1, 	au_3)$. We thus conclude that $\hat{g}(	heta_n) > \Delta_0$ for any $n \in [	au_{1}, 	au_3)$. } Next, by the definition of the stopping times $	au_{3i}$ and $	au_{3i+1}$, $ orall\ n \in [	au_{3i}, 	au_{3i+1})$ ($i \geq 1$), we have  egin{align} \hat{g}(	heta_{n}) \leq \Delta_0.\ \,\, \end{align} Meanwhile, the stopping time $	au_{3i-1} > 	au_{3i-2}$ holds for $i\ge 2$, because for any $\ i\ge 2$ we have \[ \Delta_{0} < \hat{g}(	heta_{	au_{3i-2}}) \le \hat{g}(	heta_{	au_{3i-2}-1}) + h(\hat{g}(	heta_{	au_{3i-2}-1})) \le \Delta_{0} + h(\Delta_{0}) \mathop{<}^{(a)}  rac{3\Delta_{0}}{2} < 2\Delta_{0}, \] where $(a)$ is due to our choice of $\Delta_{0} > C_{0}$ such that $h(\Delta_{0}) <  rac{\Delta_{0}}{2}$ (\cref{lem:adj:ghat}). By the \emph{Lebesgue's monotone convergence} theorem, \(\mathbb{E}\left[\sup_{n \ge 1} g(	heta_{n}) ight]\) is also controlled by this bound. 
oindent{ f Phase II:} In this step, for any $T \geq 1$, our aim is to estimate $\mathbb{E}[\sup_{1\le n<T}g(	heta_{n})]$ based on the segment of $g$ on the stopping time $	au_t$ defined in the Phase I. For any $T \geq 1$, we define $	au_{t,T} = 	au_t \wedge T$. Specifically, we conclude the following auxiliary lemma, whose proof is provided in \cref{appendix:add:proof}.  egin{lem} For the stopping time sequence defined in \cref{stopping_time} and the intervals $I_{1,	au}=[	au_{1,T}, 	au_{3,T})$ and $I_{i,	au}^{'}=[	au_{3i-1,T}, 	au_{3i,T})$, we have  egin{align} & \mathbb{E}\Big[\sup_{1\le n< T}g(	heta_{n})\Big] 
otag \ \le&\ \overline{C}_{\Pi,0}+ C_{\Pi,1}C_{\Delta_{0}}\cdot\sum_{i=2}^{+\infty}\underbrace{\mathbb{E} ig[\mathbb{I}_{	au_{3i-1,T}<	au_{3i,T}} ig]}_{\Psi_{i,1}}+C_{\Pi,1}C_{\Gamma,1}\underbrace{\mathbb{E}\left[ igg(\sum_{I_{1,	au}}+\sum_{i=2}^{+\infty}\sum_{n=I_{i,	au}^{'}}  igg)\mathbb{E}[\Gamma_n|\mathscr{F}_{n-1}]ight]}_{\Psi_{2}} 
otag \&+C_{\Pi,1}C_{\Gamma,2}\underbrace{\mathbb{E}\Bigg[ igg(\sum_{n=I_{1,	au}}+\sum_{i=2}^{+\infty}\sum_{n=I_{i,	au}^{'}}  igg) rac{\Gamma_{n}}{\sqrt{S_{n}}}\Bigg]}_{\Psi_{3}}, \end{align} where $\overline{C}_{\Pi,0}:=\hat{g}(	heta_{1})+ rac{3\Delta_{0}}{2}+C_{\Pi,0}$, $C_{\Pi,0},\ C_{\Pi,1}$ and $C_{\Delta_{0}}$ are constants defined in \cref{constant_Pi} and \cref{inequ:C:Delta0} respectively, and $C_{\Gamma,1}, C_{\Gamma,2}$ are constants defined in \cref{sufficient:lem}. \end{lem}

otag \ &\mathop{=}^{(a)} \mathbb{E}\Bigg[ igg(\sum_{n=I_{1,	au}}+\sum_{i=2}^{+\infty}\sum_{n=I_{i,	au}^{'}}  igg)\mathbb{I}_{\|

abla g(	heta_{n})\|^{2} > \eta$ for any $ n \in I_{1,	au} \cup I_{i,	au}^{'}$ (by \cref{pro_0}). otag \&+  rac{4C_{\Gamma,2}}{\Delta_0}\sum_{i=2}^{+\infty}\mathbb{E}\Bigg[\sum_{n=	au_{3i-2,T}}^{	au_{3i-1,T}-1} rac{\Gamma_{n}}{\sqrt{S_{n}}}\Bigg] +  rac{4\alpha_0^{2}}{\Delta_0^{2}}\sum_{i=2}^{+\infty}\mathbb{E}\Bigg[ \sum_{n=	au_{3i-2,T}}^{	au_{3i-1,T}-1}\hat{X}_{n}^{2} igg]. \end{align} First, we bound the first term on the RHS of \cref{power_01}. When the interval $[	au_{3i-2,T}, 	au_{3i-1,T})$ is non-degenerated (i.e., $	au_{3i-2} < 	au_{3i-1}$), we must have $\hat{g}(	heta_{n}) > \Delta_0 \geq \hat{C}_{g}$. By \cref{pro_0} we have $\|
abla g(	heta_{n})\|^{2} > \eta$ for any $n \in [	au_{3i-2,T}, 	au_{3i-1,T})$. abla g(	heta_{n})\|^{2}>\eta} rac{\|
abla g(	heta_{n},\xi_{n})\|^{2}}{S_{n}} igg]ight]

otag\& \le\ 2\sum_{i=2}^{+\infty}\mathbb{E}\Bigg[\sum_{n=	au_{3i-2,T}}^{	au_{3i-1,T}-1}\|
abla g(	heta_{n})\|^{2}\Gamma_{n}+ igg( rac{\sigma_{1}}{2\sqrt{S_{0}}}\Gamma^{2}_{n}+ rac{\sigma_{0}}{2}\Lambda_{n}^{2} igg)^{2}\Bigg]
otag\ & \mathop{\leq}^{(a)}\ 2\Big(4{ L\Delta_0}+ rac{\sigma_{1}}{2\sqrt{S_{0}}}+ rac{\sigma_{0}}{8}\Big)\sum_{i=2}^{+\infty}\mathbb{E}\Bigg[\sum_{n=	au_{3i-2,T}}^{	au_{3i-1,T}-1}\Gamma_{n}\Bigg]
otag\ &\mathop{=}^{(b)}\ 2\Big(4{ L\Delta_0}+ rac{\sigma_{1}}{2\sqrt{S_{0}}}+ rac{\sigma_{0}}{8}\Big)\sum_{i=2}^{+\infty}\mathbb{E} igg[\sum_{n=	au_{3i-2,T}}^{	au_{3i-1,T}-1}\mathbb{I}_{\|
abla g(	heta_{n})\|^{2}>\eta} rac{\|
abla g(	heta_{n},\xi_{n})\|^{2}}{{S_{n}}}  igg]
otag\ & \leq \ 2\Big(4{ L\Delta_0}+ rac{\sigma_{1}}{2\sqrt{S_{0}}}+ rac{\sigma_{0}}{8}\Big)\sum_{i=2}^{+\infty}\mathbb{E} igg[\sum _{n=	au_{3i-2,T}}^{	au_{3i-1,T}-1}\mathbb{I}_{\|
abla g(	heta_{n})\|^{2}>\eta} rac{\|
abla g(	heta_{n},\xi_{n})\|^{2}}{{S_{n-1}}}  igg]
otag\ &\mathop{<}^{	ext{\cref{lem_su}}}\ 2\Big(4{ L\Delta_0}+ rac{\sigma_{1}}{2\sqrt{S_{0}}}+ rac{\sigma_{0}}{8}\Big) \left(\sigma_0 +  rac{\sigma_1}{\eta} ight)M, \end{align} where $(a)$ is due to when $n\in[	au_{3i-2,T},	au_{3i-1,T}),$ there is $\|
abla g(	heta_{n})\|^{2} \leq 2 Lg(	heta_n) \leq {4 L\Delta_0},$ and $\Lambda_{n}\le  rac{1}{2}\Gamma_{n}$; $(b)$ is because when the interval $[	au_{3i-2,T}, 	au_{3i-1,T})$ is non-degenerated (i.e., $	au_{3i-2} < 	au_{3i-1}$), we have $\hat{g}(	heta_{n}) > \Delta_0 \geq \hat{C}_{g}$. abla g(	heta_{n})\|^{2} > \eta$ for any $n \in [	au_{3i-2,T}, 	au_{3i-1,T})$. Substituting \cref{jrnn_00}, \cref{jrnn_01}, and \cref{jrnn_02} into \cref{power_01} yields  egin{equation}
onumber egin{aligned} \sum_{i=2}^{+\infty}\Psi_{i,1}&<  rac{4C_{\Gamma,1}}{\Delta_0}\left(\sigma_0 + \sigma_1/\eta ight) M +  rac{4C_{\Gamma,2}}{\Delta_0} rac{2}{\sqrt{S_0}}\& +  rac{4\alpha_0^2}{\Delta_0^2} 2\left(4 L\Delta_0+ rac{\sigma_{1}}{2\sqrt{S_{0}}}+ rac{\sigma_{0}}{8}ight) \left(\sigma_0 +  rac{\sigma_1}{\eta} ight)M :=\overline{M}, \end{aligned}\end{equation} which means there exists a constant $\overline{M} < +\infty$ such that $\sum_{i=2}^{+\infty}\Psi_{i,1}<\overline{M}$. Combining the above estimation of $\sum_{i=2}^{+\infty}\Psi_{i,1}$ and estimations of $\Psi_2$ and $\Psi_3$ in \cref{inequ:phi_2,inequ:phi_3} into \cref{lem:inequ:supg:main}, we have  egin{equation}
onumber egin{aligned} \mathbb{E}\Big[\sup_{1\le n<T}g(	heta_{n})\Big]&< \overline{C}_{\Pi,0} + C_{\Pi,1}C_{\Delta_0} \overline{M} + C_{\Pi,1}C_{\Gamma,1}\left(\sigma_0 +  rac{\sigma_1}{\eta} ight)M + C_{\Pi,1}C_{\Gamma,2}  rac{2}{\sqrt{S_0}}\&:=\overline{M}_{1}<+\infty. \end{aligned}\end{equation} Therefore, there exists a constant $\overline{M}_{1} < +\infty$ that is independent on $T$ such that $\mathbb{E}\Big[\sup_{1\le n<T}g(	heta_{n})\Big]<+\infty$. nodes.statement: Thus, the outliers only appear between the stopping times \([ \tau_{3i-1}, \tau_{3i})\). nodes.name: Conclude stability
nodes.statement: Combining the above estimation of $\sum_{i=2}^{+\infty}\Psi_{i,1}$ and estimations of $\Psi_2$ and $\Psi_3$ in \cref{inequ:phi_2,inequ:phi_3} into \cref{lem:inequ:supg:main}, we have \begin{equation}\nonumber\begin{aligned} \mathbb{E}\Big[\sup_{1\le n<T}g(\theta_{n})\Big]&< \overline{C}_{\Pi,0} + C_{\Pi,1}C_{\Delta_0} \overline{M} + C_{\Pi,1}C_{\Gamma,1}\left(\sigma_0 + \frac{\sigma_1}{\eta} \right)M + C_{\Pi,1}C_{\Gamma,2} \frac{2}{\sqrt{S_0}}\\&:=\overline{M}_{1}<+\infty. \end{aligned}\end{equation} Therefore, there exists a constant $\overline{M}_{1} < +\infty$ that is independent on $T$ such that $\mathbb{E}\Big[\sup_{1\le n<T}g(\theta_{n})\Big]<+\infty$. Since \(\overline{M}_{1}\) is independent of \(T\), according to the \emph{ Lebesgue's monotone convergence} theorem, we have $\mathbb{E}\Big[\sup_{n\ge 1}g(\theta_{n})\Big]<\overline{M}_{1}<+\infty,$ as we desired.
nodes.statement_short: Uniform bound plus monotone convergence give the theorem

nodes.name: Coercivity and weak Sard condition
nodes.statement: \begin{enumerate}[label=\textnormal{(\roman*)}, leftmargin=*] \item (\textbf{Coercivity}) The function $g$ is coercive, that is, $\lim_{\|\theta\|\rightarrow+\infty} g(\theta) = +\infty$. \item (\textbf{Weak Sard Condition}) The critical value set $\{g(\theta) \mid \nabla g(\theta) = 0\}$ is nowhere dense in $\mathbb{R}$. \end{enumerate}
nodes.label: extra

nodes.name: Weak Sard condition from differentiability and bounded critical set
nodes.statement: Suppose that $f:\mathbb{R}^{d}\rightarrow\mathbb{R}$ is $d$-time differentiable and the critical points set $J$ is bounded where $J:=\{\theta \mid \nabla f(\theta)=0\}$. Then, the critical values set $f(J_{f}):=\{f(\theta) \mid \nabla f(\theta)=0\}$, are nowhere dense in $\mathbb{R}$.
assumptions: the critical points set $J$ is bounded where $J:=\{\theta \mid \nabla f(\theta)=0\}$
conclusions: the critical values set $f(J_{f}):=\{f(\theta) \mid \nabla f(\theta)=0\}$, are nowhere dense in $\mathbb{R}$
nodes.label: pros:assump:loss

nodes.name: Proof of Claim 1
nodes.statement: Since the critical point set $J$ is bounded, the critical values set $f(J_{f})$ is closed. Suppose that there exists an interval $(a, b)$ such that the set $f(J_{f})$ is dense on this interval. This condition is both necessary and sufficient to guarantee $f(J_{f})$ to have an interior point. Given that $f$ is $d$-times differentiable, we can apply \textit{Sard's theorem} \citep{sard1942measure,bates1993toward} and deduce that $m(f(J_{f}))=0,$ where $m(\cdot)$ denotes \textit{Lebesgue's Measure}. It is well known that a set containing an interior point cannot have a zero measure. Thus, we conclude that $f(J_{f})$ is nowhere dense in $\mathbb{R}.$
nodes.statement_short: By contradiction with Sard's theorem: an interior point would give positive measure.

nodes.name: Closedness
nodes.statement: Since the critical point set $J$ is bounded, the critical values set $f(J_{f})$ is closed.

nodes.name: Assume interior point
nodes.statement: Suppose that there exists an interval $(a, b)$ such that the set $f(J_{f})$ is dense on this interval. This condition is both necessary and sufficient to guarantee $f(J_{f})$ to have an interior point.
nodes.statement_short: Assume the critical values are dense on an interval

nodes.name: Apply Sard's theorem
nodes.statement: Given that $f$ is $d$-times differentiable, we can apply \textit{Sard's theorem} \citep{sard1942measure,bates1993toward} and deduce that $m(f(J_{f}))=0,$ where $m(\cdot)$ denotes \textit{Lebesgue's Measure}.
nodes.statement_short: Sard gives measure zero critical values

nodes.name: Contradiction
nodes.statement: It is well known that a set containing an interior point cannot have a zero measure. Thus, we conclude that $f(J_{f})$ is nowhere dense in $\mathbb{R}.$

nodes.name: Stability of AdaGrad-Norm iterates
nodes.statement: If \cref{ass_g_poi,ass_noise} and \cref{extra}~\ref{extra:i1} hold, given AdaGrad-Norm, we have $$\sup_{n\ge 1}\|\theta_{n}\|<+\infty\ \ \text{a.s.}$$
nodes.label: stable':iterate

nodes.name: Proof of Corollary 3.2
nodes.statement: From \cref{stable}, we obtain $\mathbb{E}[\sup_{n\ge 1}g(\theta_{n})]<+\infty,$ which implies $\sup_{n\ge 1}g(\theta_{n})<+\infty\ \ \text{a.s.}$ Then, by the \emph{coercivity}, it is evident that $\sup_{n\ge 1}\|\theta_{n}\|<+\infty\ \ \text{a.s.}$.
nodes.statement_short: Stability gives a.s. bounded loss; coercivity bounds the iterates.

nodes.name: Divergence of the sum of step sizes
nodes.statement: Consider AdaGrad-Norm, if \cref{ass_g_poi,ass_noise} hold, then we have $\sum_{n=1}^{+\infty}\frac{1}{\sqrt{S_{n}}}=+\infty \, \ \text{a.s.}$
nodes.label: step size

nodes.name: Standard stochastic approximation iteration
nodes.statement: We follow the iterative formula of the standard stochastic approximation (as discussed on page 11 of \cite{benaim2006dynamics}) \begin{align} x_{n+1} = x_{n} - \gamma_{n}(g(x_{n})+U_{n}), \end{align} where $\sum_{n=1}^{+\infty}\gamma_{n}=+\infty$ and $\lim_{n\rightarrow+\infty}\gamma_{n}=0$ and $U_n \in \mathbb{R}^d$ are the random noise (perturbations).
nodes.statement_short: Stochastic approximation $x_{n+1}=x_n-\gamma_n(g(x_n)+U_n)$ with non-summable, vanishing step sizes.

nodes.name: ODE method criterion for stochastic approximation
nodes.statement: Let $F$ be a continuous globally integrable vector field. Assume that \begin{enumerate}[label=\textnormal{(A.\arabic*)},leftmargin=*] \item Suppose $\sup_n \|x_n\|< \infty,$ \item For all $T > 0$ \[ \lim_{n \to \infty} \sup \left\lbrace \left\lVert \sum_{i=n}^{k} \gamma_{i}U_{i} \right\lVert : k = n, \dots, m(\Sigma_{\gamma}(n) + T) \right\rbrace = 0, \] where \[\Sigma_\gamma(n):=\sum_{k=1}^{n}\gamma_{k}\ \ \text{and}\ \ m(t):=\max\{j\ge 0: \Sigma_{\gamma}(j)\le t\}.\] \item \(F(V)\) is nowhere dense on \(\mathbb{R}\), where \(V\) is the fixed point set of the ODE: \(\dot{x} = g(x)\). \end{enumerate} Then all limit points of the sequence \(\{x_{n}\}_{n\ge 1}\) are fixed points of the ODE: \(\dot{x} = g(x)\).
assumptions: Let $F$ be a continuous globally integrable vector field.

For all $T > 0$ \[ \lim_{n \to \infty} \sup \left\lbrace \left\lVert \sum_{i=n}^{k} \gamma_{i}U_{i} \right\lVert : k = n, \dots, m(\Sigma_{\gamma}(n) + T) \right\rbrace = 0, \] where \[\Sigma_\gamma(n):=\sum_{k=1}^{n}\gamma_{k}\ \ \text{and}\ \ m(t):=\max\{j\ge 0: \Sigma_{\gamma}(j)\le t\}.\]
\(F(V)\) is nowhere dense on \(\mathbb{R}\), where \(V\) is the fixed point set of the ODE: \(\dot{x} = g(x)\).
conclusions: Then all limit points of the sequence \(\{x_{n}\}_{n\ge 1}\) are fixed points of the ODE: \(\dot{x} = g(x)\).
nodes.statement_short: If iterates are bounded, noise sums vanish on ODE time windows and $F(V)$ is nowhere dense, limit points are ODE equilibria.
nodes.label: SA_p

nodes.name: Sources of the ODE method criterion
nodes.statement: \cref{SA_p} synthesizes results from Proposition 4.1, Theorem 5.7, and Proposition 6.4 in \cite{benaim2006dynamics}. Proposition 4.1 shows that the trajectory of an algorithm satisfying~\cref{pros:a1,pros:a2} forms a precompact asymptotic pseudotrajectory of the corresponding ODE system. Meanwhile, Theorem 5.7 and Proposition 6.4 demonstrate that all limit points of this precompact asymptotic pseudotrajectory are fixed points of the ODE system.

nodes.name: Almost sure convergence of AdaGrad-Norm
nodes.statement: Consider the AdaGrad-Norm algorithm defined in \cref{AdaGrad_Norm}. If \cref{ass_g_poi,ass_noise,extra} hold, then for any initial point $\theta_{1}\in \mathbb{R}^{d}$ and $S_{0}>0,$ we have \begin{equation}\nonumber\begin{aligned} \lim_{n\rightarrow\infty}\|\nabla g(\theta_{n})\|=0\ \ \text{a.s.} \end{aligned}\end{equation}

nodes.name: Step-size conditions
nodes.statement: When \(\mathcal{A}^{c}\) occurs, it is clear that \(\lim_{n\rightarrow+\infty} \gamma_n = \lim_{n\rightarrow+\infty}\frac{\alpha_{0}}{\sqrt{S_{n}}}=0\). According to \cref{step size}, we know that \( \lim_{n \rightarrow \infty}\Sigma_{\gamma}(n) = \sum_{n=1}^{+\infty} \gamma_n = \sum_{n=1}^{+\infty}\frac{\alpha_{0}}{\sqrt{S_{n}}} = +\infty\ a.s.\) Therefore, it forms a standard stochastic approximation algorithm.

nodes.name: Condition A.1
nodes.statement: Next, we aim to verify the two conditions, namely \cref{pros:a1,pros:a2} of \cref{SA_p}, hold for AdaGrad-Norm and use the conclusion of \cref{SA_p} to prove the almost sure convergence of AdaGrad-Norm. Based on the stability of AdaGrad-Norm in \cref{stable':iterate}, we have \(\sup_{n\ge 1}\|\theta_{n}\|<+\infty\ a.s.\), thus Condition~\cref{pros:a1} holds.

nodes.name: Stopping times mu_t
nodes.statement: Next, we will check whether Condition \cref{pros:a2} is correct. For any \(N>0\), we define the stopping time sequence \(\{\mu_{t}\}_{t\ge 0}\) \begin{equation}\nonumber\begin{aligned} &\mu_{0}:=1,\ \mu_{1}:=\max\{n\ge 1:\Sigma_{\gamma}(n)\le N\},\ \mu_{t}:=\max\{n\ge \mu_{t-1}:\Sigma_{\gamma}(n)\le tN\}, \end{aligned}\end{equation} where $ \Sigma_{\gamma}(n):=\sum_{k=1}^{n}\frac{\alpha_{0}}{\sqrt{S_{k}}}.$ By the definition of the stopping time $\mu_{t}$, we split the value of $\left\lbrace\Sigma_{\gamma}(n) \right\rbrace_{n=1}^{\infty}$ into pieces.

nodes.name: Almost-sure vs mean-square convergence
nodes.statement: (Almost-sure vs mean-square convergence) As stated in the introduction, the almost sure convergence does not imply mean square convergence. To illustrate this concept, let us consider a sequence of random variables $\{\zeta_{n}\}_{n\ge 1},$ where $\mathbb{P}[\zeta_{n}=0]=1-1/n^{2}$ and $\mathbb{P}[\zeta_{n}=n^{2}]=1/n^{2}.$ According to \textit{the Borel-Cantelli lemma}, it follows that $\lim_{n\rightarrow+\infty}\zeta_{n}=0$ almost surely. However, it can be shown that $\mathbb{E}[\zeta_{n}]=1$ for all $n>0$ by simple calculations.

nodes.statement: Under \cref{ass_g_poi} \ref{ass_g_poi:i}$\sim$\ref{ass_g_poi:i2}, \cref{ass_noise} \ref{ass_noise:i}, \cref{coordinate} \ref{coordinate_i_1}, consider the sequence $\{\theta_{t}\}$ generated by RMSProp, we have the following sufficient decrease inequality. \begin{align} \hat{g}(\theta_{t+1})-\hat{g}(\theta_t) & \le-\frac{3}{4}\sum_{i=1}^{d}\zeta_{i}(t)+\left(\frac{ L}{2}+\frac{(2\sigma_{0}+1) L^{2}}{\sqrt{v}}\right)\|\eta_{t}\circ \nabla g(\theta_{t},\xi_{t})\|^{2}+M_{t}, \end{align} where $M_{t}:=M_{t,1}+M_{t,2}+M_{t,3}$ is a martingale difference sequence with \( M_{t,1} \) defined in \cref{adam_0} and \( M_{t,2} \), \( M_{t,3} \) defined in \cref{adam_2}.
nodes.section: 5 Extension of the Analysis to RMSProp
assumptions: consider the sequence $\{\theta_{t}\}$ generated by RMSProp
nodes.statement_short: RMSProp Lyapunov function decreases by $\tfrac34\sum_i\zeta_i(t)$ up to a squared-step term and a martingale difference.

nodes.name: Stability of RMSProp
nodes.statement: Suppose that \cref{ass_g_poi} \ref{ass_g_poi:i}$\sim$\ref{ass_g_poi:i2}, \cref{ass_noise} \ref{ass_noise:i}, \cref{coordinate_0}, \cref{coordinate} \cref{coordinate_i_1} hold. Consider RMSProp. We have \[\mathbb{E}\left[\sup_{n\ge 1}g(\theta_{n})\right] < +\infty.\]

nodes.name: Almost sure convergence of RMSProp
nodes.statement: Suppose that \cref{ass_g_poi} \ref{ass_g_poi:i}$\sim$\ref{ass_g_poi:i2}, \cref{ass_noise} \ref{ass_noise:i}, \cref{coordinate_0,coordinate,extra} hold. Consider RMSProp. We have \begin{equation}\nonumber\begin{aligned} \lim_{n\rightarrow\infty}\|\nabla g(\theta_{n})\|=0\ \ \text{a.s.} \end{aligned}\end{equation}
nodes.section: 5 Extension of the Analysis to RMSProp
nodes.label: convergence_1.0'

nodes.name: Mean-square convergence of RMSProp
nodes.statement: Suppose that \cref{ass_g_poi} \ref{ass_g_poi:i}$\sim$\ref{ass_g_poi:i2}, \cref{ass_noise} \ref{ass_noise:i}, \cref{coordinate_0,coordinate,extra} hold. Consider RMSProp. We have \begin{equation}\nonumber\begin{aligned} \lim_{n\rightarrow\infty}\mathbb{E}\|\nabla g(\theta_{n})\|^{2}=0. \end{aligned}\end{equation}
nodes.section: 5 Extension of the Analysis to RMSProp
nodes.label: convergence_2.0'

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 5.3
nodes.statement: Based on the function value's stability in \cref{bound''}, we can derive the following inequality: \[\mathbb{E}\Big[\sup_{n\ge 1}\|\nabla g(\theta_{n})\|^{2}\Big] \mathop{\le}^{\text{\cref{loss_bound}}} 2 L\mathbb{E}\Big[\sup_{n\ge 1}g(\theta_{n})\Big]<+\infty.\] Then, by the almost sure convergence from \cref{convergence_1.0'} and \emph{Lebesgue's dominated convergence} theorem, the mean-square convergence result, i.e., \(\lim_{n\rightarrow\infty}\mathbb{E}\|\nabla g(\theta_{n})\|^{2}=0\) follows.
nodes.section: 5 Extension of the Analysis to RMSProp
nodes.statement_short: Dominated convergence using RMSProp stability and a.s. convergence.

nodes.name: Non-asymptotic rate for RMSProp
nodes.statement: It is worth mentioning that our approach for establishing the non-asymptotic convergence rate of AdaGrad-Norm can be directly applied to RMSProp under the hyperparameters setting in \cref{near_optimal_para}, which implies \(\frac{1}{T} \sum_{t=1}^{T} \mathbb{E}\|\nabla g(\theta_{n})\|^2 \leq \mathcal{O}(\ln T/\sqrt{T})\).

nodes.name: Gradient norm bound for smooth lower-bounded functions
nodes.statement: (Lemma 10 of \cite{jin2022convergence}) Suppose that $g(x)$ is differentiable and lower bounded $ g^{\ast} = \inf_{x\in \ \mathbb{R}^{d}}g(x) >-\infty$ and $\nabla g(x)$ is Lipschitz continuous with parameter $ L > 0$, then $\forall \ x\in \ \mathbb{R}^{d}$, we have \begin{align*} \big\|\nabla g(x)\big\|^{2}\le {2 L}\big(g(x)-g^{*}\big). \end{align*}

Then it holds that $\sum_{k=0}^{+\infty}Y_k<+\infty \ a.s.,$ if there exists $p\in (0,2)$ such that \begin{align*} \sum_{n=1}^{+\infty}\mathbb{E}[\|Y_{n}\|^{p}]<+\infty, \quad \text{ or } \quad \sum_{n=1}^{+\infty}\mathbb{E}\big[\|Y_{n}\|^{p}\big|\mathscr{F}_{n-1}\big]<+\infty. \quad \text{a.s.} \end{align*}

nodes.name: Summability of non-negative random series
nodes.statement: (Lemma 6 in \cite{jin2022convergence}) Suppose that $\{Y_n\}\in \mathbb{R}^{d}$ is a non-negative sequence of random variables, then it holds that $\sum_{n=0}^{+\infty} Y_n<+\infty \ a.s.,$ if\ $\sum_{n=0}^{+\infty}\mathbb{E}\big[Y_n\big]<+\infty.$

nodes.name: Growth rate of martingale transforms
nodes.statement: (Lemma 4.2.13 in \cite{Guo2005}) Let $\{Y_{n},\mathscr{F}_{n}\}$ be a martingale difference sequence, where $Y_n$ can be a matrix. Let $(U_{n},\mathscr{F}_{n})$ be an adapted process, where $U_{n}$ can be a matrix, and $\|U_{n}\|<+\infty$ almost surely for all $n$. If $\sup_{n}\mathbb{E}[\|Y_{n+1}\||\mathscr{F}_{n}]<+\infty\ \ a.s.,$ then we have $$\sum_{k=0}^{n}U_{n}Y_{n+1}=\mathcal{O}\bigg(\bigg(\sum_{k=0}^{n}\|U_{n}\|\bigg)\ln^{1+\sigma}\Bigg(\bigg(\sum_{k=0}^{n}\|U_{n}\|\bigg)+e\Bigg)\Bigg)\ \ (\forall\ \sigma>0)\ \ \text{a.s.}$$

assumptions: Let $\{Y_{n},\mathscr{F}_{n}\}$ be a martingale difference sequence, where $Y_n$ can be a matrix. Let $(U_{n},\mathscr{F}_{n})$ be an adapted process, where $U_{n}$ can be a matrix, and $\|U_{n}\|<+\infty$ almost surely for all $n$.

nodes.name: Burkholder's inequality
nodes.statement: (Burkholder's inequality) Let \( \{X_n\}_{n \geq 0} \) be a real-valued martingale difference sequence for a filtration \( \{\mathscr{F}_n\}_{n \geq 0} \), and let \( s\le t<+\infty \) be two stopping time with respect to the same filtration \( \{\mathscr{F}_n\}_{n \geq 0} \). Then for any \( p > 1 \), there exist positive constants \( C_p \) and \( C_p' \) (depending only on \( p \)) such that \[C_p \mathbb{E}\left[\bigg(\sum_{n=s}^{t}|X_{n}|^{2}\bigg)^{p/2}\right] \leq \mathbb{E}\left[\sup_{s \leq n \leq t} \bigg|\sum_{k=s}^{n}X_k\bigg|^{p} \right] \leq C_p' \mathbb{E}\left[\bigg(\sum_{n=s}^{t}|X_{n}|^{2}\bigg)^{p/2}\right].\]

assumptions: Let \( \{X_n\}_{n \geq 0} \) be a real-valued martingale difference sequence for a filtration \( \{\mathscr{F}_n\}_{n \geq 0} \), and let \( s\le t<+\infty \) be two stopping time with respect to the same filtration \( \{\mathscr{F}_n\}_{n \geq 0} \).
conclusions: there exist positive constants \( C_p \) and \( C_p' \) (depending only on \( p \)) such that \[C_p \mathbb{E}\left[\bigg(\sum_{n=s}^{t}|X_{n}|^{2}\bigg)^{p/2}\right] \leq \mathbb{E}\left[\sup_{s \leq n \leq t} \bigg|\sum_{k=s}^{n}X_k\bigg|^{p} \right] \leq C_p' \mathbb{E}\left[\bigg(\sum_{n=s}^{t}|X_{n}|^{2}\bigg)^{p/2}\right].\]
nodes.label: vital2

nodes.name: Doob's stopped theorem
nodes.statement: (Doob's stopped theorem) For an adapted process $(Y_{n}, \mathscr{F}_{n})$, if there exist two bounded stopping times $s \leq t < +\infty\ a.s.$, and if $[s= n] \in \mathscr{F}_{n-1}$ and $[t=n]\in \mathscr{F}_{n-1}$ for all $n > 0$, then the following equation holds. \[ \mathbb{E}\left[\sum_{n=s}^{t}Y_{n}\right] = \mathbb{E}\left[\sum_{n=s}^{t}\mathbb{E}[Y_{n}|\mathscr{F}_{n-1}]\right]. \]

nodes.name: Expectation of sums between stopping times
nodes.statement: For an adapted process $(Y_{n}, \mathscr{F}_{n})$, and finite stopping times \(a-1,\) \(a\) and \(b\), i.e., $a,\ b<+\infty\ a.s.$ the following equation holds. \begin{align*} \mathbb{E}\left[\sum_{n=a}^b Y_n \right] = \mathbb{E}\left[\sum_{n=a}^{b}\mathbb{E}[ Y_n|\mathscr{F}_{n-1}] \right]. \end{align*}
nodes.section: A Appendix: Auxiliary Lemmas for the Theoretical Results

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma A.7
nodes.statement: (of \cref{sum:expect:ab}) \begin{align*} \mathbb{E}\left[\sum_{n=a}^b Y_n \right]&=\mathbb{E}\left[\sum_{n=1}^{b}Y_{n}-\sum_{n=1}^{a-1}Y_{n}\right]=\mathbb{E}\left[\sum_{n=1}^{b}Y_{n}\right]-\mathbb{E}\left[\sum_{n=1}^{a-1}Y_{n}\right]\\&\mathop{=}^{(a)}\mathbb{E}\left[\sum_{n=1}^{b}\mathbb{E}\left[Y_{n}|\mathscr{F}_{n-1}\right]\right]-\mathbb{E}\left[\sum_{n=1}^{a-1}\mathbb{E}\left[Y_{n}|\mathscr{F}_{n-1}\right]\right]\\&=\mathbb{E}\left[\sum_{n=a}^b \mathbb{E}[Y_n|\mathscr{F}_{n-1}] \right], \end{align*} where in \emph{$(a)$}, we apply \emph{Doob's stopped} theorem, i.e., for any stopping times \(s < +\infty\ \ a.s.\), we have \(\mathbb{E}\left[\sum_{n=1}^{s} Y_n\right] = \mathbb{E}\left[\sum_{n=1}^{s} \mathbb{E}[Y_n|\mathscr{F}_{n-1}]\right].\)

nodes.statement: For the first term of RHS of \cref{inequ:sequence:1}, since $\hat{g}(\theta_n) = g(\theta_n) + \sigma_0\alpha_0\zeta(n)/2 \geq 0$ for all $n \geq 1$, we have \begin{align} & \sum_{n=1}^{T}\frac{1}{n^{2}}\big(\hat{g}(\theta_{n})-\hat{g}(\theta_{n+1})\big) = \sum_{n=1}^{T} \frac{\hat{g}(\theta_{n})}{n^2}-\frac{\hat{g}(\theta_{n+1})}{(n+1)^2} + \frac{\hat{g}(\theta_{n+1})}{(n+1)^{2}} - \frac{\hat{g}(\theta_{n+1})}{n^{2}} \notag \\ = &\sum_{n=1}^{T} \frac{\hat{g}(\theta_{n})}{n^2}-\frac{\hat{g}(\theta_{n+1})}{(n+1)^2} - \frac{\hat{g}(\theta_{n+1})(2n+1)}{(n+1)^{2}n^2} \leq \hat{g}(\theta_1). \end{align}
nodes.section: A Appendix: Auxiliary Lemmas for the Theoretical Results
nodes.statement_short: Weighted telescoping sum bounded by $\hat g(\theta_1)$

nodes.statement: & \sum_{n=1}^{T}\frac{1}{n^{2}}\big(\hat{g}(\theta_{n})-\hat{g}(\theta_{n+1})\big) = \sum_{n=1}^{T} \frac{\hat{g}(\theta_{n})}{n^2}-\frac{\hat{g}(\theta_{n+1})}{(n+1)^2} + \frac{\hat{g}(\theta_{n+1})}{(n+1)^{2}} - \frac{\hat{g}(\theta_{n+1})}{n^{2}} \notag \\ = &\sum_{n=1}^{T} \frac{\hat{g}(\theta_{n})}{n^2}-\frac{\hat{g}(\theta_{n+1})}{(n+1)^2} - \frac{\hat{g}(\theta_{n+1})(2n+1)}{(n+1)^{2}n^2} \leq \hat{g}(\theta_1).
nodes.section: A Appendix: Auxiliary Lemmas for the Theoretical Results

nodes.name: Series-integral
nodes.statement: For the second term of RHS of \cref{inequ:sequence:1}, we utilized the series-integral result \[\sum_{n=1}^{T}\frac{\|\nabla g(\theta_{n},\xi_{n})\|^{2}}{n^2 S_{n}^{\frac{3}{2}}} \leq \sum_{n=1}^{T}\frac{\|\nabla g(\theta_{n},\xi_{n})\|^{2}}{S_{n}^{\frac{3}{2}}}<\int_{S_{0}}^{+\infty}\frac{1}{x^{\frac{3}{2}}}\text{d}x=\frac{2}{\sqrt{S_{0}}}.\]
nodes.section: A Appendix: Auxiliary Lemmas for the Theoretical Results

nodes.name: Expectation bound
nodes.statement: Applying the above estimations into \cref{inequ:sequence:1} and taking the mathematical expectation on both sides, we have $\forall\ n\ge 1,$ \begin{align} \sum_{n=1}^{T}\frac{\mathbb{E}\left[\zeta(n)\right]}{2n^2} &\le \frac{4}{\alpha_0} \hat{g}(\theta_1) + \frac{2}{\sqrt{S_0}}\mathcal{C}_1 + 4\sum_{n=1}^{T}\frac{\mathbb{E}[\hat{X}_{n}]}{n^{2}} = \frac{4}{\alpha_0} \hat{g}(\theta_1) + \frac{2}{\sqrt{S_0}}\mathcal{C}_1, \end{align} since $\lbrace \hat{X}_{n}, \mathscr{F}_{n-1}\rbrace$ is a martingale difference sequence.

nodes.statement: \sum_{n=1}^{T}\frac{\mathbb{E}\left[\zeta(n)\right]}{2n^2} &\le \frac{4}{\alpha_0} \hat{g}(\theta_1) + \frac{2}{\sqrt{S_0}}\mathcal{C}_1 + 4\sum_{n=1}^{T}\frac{\mathbb{E}[\hat{X}_{n}]}{n^{2}} = \frac{4}{\alpha_0} \hat{g}(\theta_1) + \frac{2}{\sqrt{S_0}}\mathcal{C}_1,

nodes.name: Affine noise lower bound
nodes.statement: According to \emph{the affine noise variance condition}, we obtain: \begin{align} \sum_{n=1}^{T}\frac{\mathbb{E}\left[\zeta(n)\right]}{2n^2}\ge \sum_{n=1}^{T}\frac{\mathbb{E}\left[\|\nabla g(\theta_{n},\xi_{n})\|^{2}\right]}{2\sigma_{0}n^2}-\frac{\sigma_{1}}{2\sigma_{0}}\sum_{n=1}^{T}\frac{1}{n^{2}}\mathop{\ge}^{(a)} \sum_{n=1}^{T}\frac{\mathbb{E}\left[\|\nabla g(\theta_{n},\xi_{n})\|^{2}\right]}{2\sigma_{0}n^2}-\frac{\sigma_{1}\pi^{2}}{12\sigma_{0}}. \end{align} Here, $(a)$ uses the inequity \[\sum_{n=1}^{T}\frac{1}{n^{2}}<\sum_{n=1}^{+\infty}\frac{1}{n^{2}}=\frac{\pi^{2}}{6}.\]

nodes.statement_short: Lower bound by stochastic gradient norms

Telescoping the above inequality over $n$ from the interval \(I_{1,	au}:=[	au_{1,T},	au_{3,T}-1]\) gives  egin{align*}  rac{\alpha_{0}}{4}\sum_{n \in I_{1,	au}}\zeta(n)&\le \hat{g}(	heta_{	au_{1,T}})-\hat{g}(	heta_{	au_{3,T}})+C_{\Gamma,1}\sum_{n \in I_{1,	au}} \Gamma_n+C_{\Gamma,2}\sum_{n \in I_{1,	au}} rac{\Gamma_{n}}{\sqrt{S_{n}}}+\alpha_0 \sum_{n \in I_{1,	au}}\hat{X}_{n}. \end{align*} Taking the expectation on both sides of the above inequality, we have  egin{align*}  rac{\alpha_{0}}{4}\mathbb{E}\left[\sum_{n \in I_{1,	au}}\zeta(n)ight]&\le\mathbb{E} ig[\hat{g}(	heta_{	au_{1,T}}) ig]+C_{\Gamma,1}\mathbb{E} igg[\sum_{n \in I_{1,	au}} \Gamma_n  igg]+C_{\Gamma,2}\mathbb{E}\Bigg[\sum_{n \in I_{1,	au}} rac{\Gamma_{n}}{\sqrt{S_{n}}}\Bigg]+\alpha_0\mathbb{E}\Bigg[\sum_{n \in I_{1,	au}}\hat{X}_{n}\Bigg]

For the first term of the RHS of the above inequality,  egin{align*} \mathbb{E} ig[\hat{g}(	heta_{	au_{1,T}}) ig]&=\mathbb{E} ig[\mathbb{I}_{[	au_{1}=1]}\hat{g}(	heta_{1}) ig]+\mathbb{E} ig[\mathbb{I}_{	au_{1}>1}\hat{g}(	heta_{	au_{1,T}}) ig] \&\le \hat{g}(	heta_{1})+ \mathbb{E} ig[\mathbb{I}_{	au_{1}>1}\hat{g}(	heta_{	au_{1,T}-1}) ig]+\mathbb{E} ig[\mathbb{I}_{	au_{1}>1}(\hat{g}(	heta_{	au_{1,T}})-\hat{g}(	heta_{	au_{1,T}-1})) ig]\&\mathop{\le}^{	ext{\cref{lem:adj:ghat}}} \hat{g}(	heta_{1})+\Delta_{0}+h(\Delta_{0})<\hat{g}(	heta_{1})+ rac{3\Delta_{0}}{2}. \end{align*} We thus conclude that  egin{align}  rac{\alpha_{0}}{4}\mathbb{E}\left[\sum_{n \in I_{	au,1}}\zeta(n)ight]&\le\hat{g}(	heta_{1})+ rac{3\Delta_{0}}{2}+C_{\Gamma,1}\mathbb{E} igg[\sum_{n \in I_{	au,i}} \mathbb{E}[\Gamma_n|\mathscr{F}_{n-1}]  igg]+C_{\Gamma,2}\mathbb{E}\Bigg[\sum_{n \in I_{	au,i}} rac{\Gamma_{n}}{\sqrt{S_{n}}}\Bigg]. \end{align} For the second term of $\Pi_{3,T}$, we telescope the sufficient decrease inequality in \cref{sufficient:lem} over $n$ from the interval \( I_{i,	au}^{'}:= [	au_{3i-1,T}, 	au_{3i,T}-1 ]\ ( orall\ i\ge 2)\)  egin{align}  rac{\alpha_{0}}{4}\sum_{n \in I_{i,	au}^{'}}\zeta(n)&\le \hat{g}(	heta_{	au_{3i-1,T}})-\hat{g}(	heta_{	au_{3i,T}})+C_{\Gamma,1}\sum_{n \in I_{i,	au}^{'}} \Gamma_n+C_{\Gamma,2}\sum_{n \in I_{i,	au}^{'}} rac{\Gamma_{n}}{\sqrt{S_{n}}}+\alpha_0 \sum_{n \in I_{i,	au}^{'}}\hat{X}_{n}. \end{align} Recalling the definition of the stopping time $	au_t$, we know that \(	au_{3i,T} \geq 	au_{3i-1,T}\) always holds. In particular, \(	au_{3i,T} = 	au_{3i-1,T}\) implies that \(	au_{3i,T}-1 < 	au_{3i-1,T}\). Since $\sum_{n=a}^b(\cdot) = 0$ for $b < a$, we have $\sum_{n=	au_{3i-1,T}}^{	au_{3i,T}-1}(\cdot) = 0 $ and $\hat{g}(	heta_{	au_{3i,T}}) = \hat{g}(	heta_{	au_{3i-1,T}})$, then LHS and RHS of \cref{inequ:stab:2} are both zero and \cref{inequ:stab:2} holds. Taking the expectation on both sides and noting the equation of \cref{sum:expect:ab} gives  egin{align}  rac{\alpha_{0}}{4}\mathbb{E}\left[\sum_{n \in I_{i,	au}^{'}}\zeta(n)ight]&\le \mathbb{E} ig[\hat{g}(	heta_{	au_{3i-1,T}})-\hat{g}(	heta_{	au_{3i,T}}) ig]+C_{\Gamma,1}\mathbb{E} igg[\sum_{n \in I_{i,	au}^{'}} \mathbb{E}[\Gamma_n|\mathscr{F}_{n-1}]  igg]
otag\&+C_{\Gamma,2}\mathbb{E}\Bigg[\sum_{n \in I_{i,	au}^{'}} rac{\Gamma_{n}}{\sqrt{S_{n}}}\Bigg]+0. \end{align} If \(	au_{3i-1, T} < 	au_{3i, T}\), for any $n \in I_{i,	au}^{'} = [	au_{3i-1,T}, 	au_{3i,T}-1]$, by applying \cref{lem:adj:ghat} we have  egin{align*} \hat{g}(	heta_{	au_{3i-1, T}}) - \hat{g}(	heta_{	au_{3i,T}})&<\hat{g}(	heta_{	au_{3i-1,T}}) < \hat{g}(	heta_{	au_{3i-1,T}-1})+h(\hat{g}(	heta_{	au_{3i-1,T}-1})). \end{align*} Based on the properties of the stopping time \(	au_{3i-1},\) we have $\hat{g}(	heta_{	au_{3i-1,T}-1}) \leq 2\Delta_{0}.$ Based on the above inequality, we further estimate the first term of \cref{inequ:stat:1} and achieve that  egin{align}  rac{\alpha_{0}}{4}\mathbb{E}\Bigg[\sum_{n=I_{i,	au}^{'}}\zeta(n)\Bigg]
otag&\le C_{\Delta_{0}}\mathbb{E} ig[\mathbb{I}_{\{	au_{3i-1,T}<	au_{3i,T} \}} ig]+C_{\Gamma,1}\mathbb{E} igg[\sum_{n=I_{i,	au}^{'}} \mathbb{E}[\Gamma_n|\mathscr{F}_{n-1}]  igg] \&+C_{\Gamma,2}\mathbb{E}\Bigg[\sum_{n=I_{i,	au}^{'}} rac{\Gamma_{n}}{\sqrt{S_{n}}}\Bigg] , \end{align} where  egin{align} C_{\Delta_{0}}: =2\Delta_{0}+ \sqrt{2 L}\left(1 +  rac{\sigma_0 L}{2\sqrt{S_0}}ight)\alpha_0\sqrt{2\Delta_0} + \left(1 +  rac{\sigma_0\alpha_0 L}{2\sqrt{S_0}}ight) rac{ L\alpha_0^2}{2}. \end{align} Telescoping \cref{wxm_90} over $i$ from \(2\) to \(+\infty\) to estimate the second part of $\Pi_{3,T}$, we have  egin{align}  rac{\alpha_{0}}{4}\mathbb{E}\left[\sum_{i=2}^{+\infty}\sum_{n=I_{i,	au}^{'}}\zeta(n)ight]\le& C_{\Delta_{0}}\cdot\sum_{i=2}^{+\infty}\mathbb{E} ig[\mathbb{I}_{	au_{3i-1,T}<	au_{3i,T}} ig]+C_{\Gamma,1}\sum_{i=2}^{+\infty}\mathbb{E} igg[\sum_{n=I_{i,	au}^{'}} \mathbb{E}[\Gamma_n|\mathscr{F}_{n-1}] igg] 
otag \&+C_{\Gamma,2}\sum_{i=2}^{+\infty}\mathbb{E}\Bigg[\sum_{n=I_{i,	au}^{'}} rac{\Gamma_{n}}{\sqrt{S_{n}}}\Bigg]. \end{align} Note that the stopping time \(	au_{t}\) is truncated for any finite time \(T\). For a specific $T$, the sum \(\sum_{i=2}^{+\infty}\) has only finite non-zero terms, thus we can interchange the order of summation and expectation \(\mathbb{E}\left(\sum_{i=2}^{+\infty} (\cdot) ight) = \sum_{i=2}^{+\infty} \left(\mathbb{E}(\cdot) ight).\) Substituting \cref{pqwe_1} and \cref{inequ:stat:1'} into \cref{wxm_200} gives  egin{align} &\mathbb{E}\Big[\sup_{1\le n< T}g(	heta_{n})\Big]
otag \ \le&\ \overline{C}_{\Pi,0}+ C_{\Pi,1}C_{\Delta_{0}}\cdot\sum_{i=2}^{+\infty}\underbrace{\mathbb{E} ig[\mathbb{I}_{	au_{3i-1,T}<	au_{3i,T}} ig]}_{\Psi_{i,1}}+C_{\Pi,1}C_{\Gamma,1}\underbrace{\mathbb{E}\left[ igg(\sum_{I_{1,	au}}+\sum_{i=2}^{+\infty}\sum_{n=I_{i,	au}^{'}}  igg)\mathbb{E}[\Gamma_n|\mathscr{F}_{n-1}]ight]}_{\Psi_{2}} 
otag \&\quad +C_{\Pi,1}C_{\Gamma,2}\underbrace{\mathbb{E}\Bigg[ igg(\sum_{n=I_{1,	au}}+\sum_{i=2}^{+\infty}\sum_{n=I_{i,	au}^{'}}  igg) rac{\Gamma_{n}}{\sqrt{S_{n}}}\Bigg]}_{\Psi_{3}}, \end{align} where $\overline{C}_{\Pi,0}:=\hat{g}(	heta_{1})+ rac{3\Delta_{0}}{2}+C_{\Pi,0}.$

nodes.name: Combine Pi bounds
nodes.statement: By substituting the estimations of $\Pi_{2,T}^1$ and $\Pi_{2,T}^2$ from \cref{inequ:xt21} and \cref{qaswert} respectively into \cref{inequ:xt2}, we achieve the estimation for $\Pi_{2,T}$. Then, substituting the result for $\Pi_{2,T}$ into \cref{start} gives \begin{align} \mathbb{E}\Big[\sup_{1\le n<T}g(\theta_{n})\Big]\le C_{\Pi,0}+C_{\Pi, 1}\underbrace{\mathbb{E}\Bigg[\sum_{n=\tau_{1,T}}^{\tau_{3,T}-1}\zeta(n)+\sum_{i=2}^{+\infty}\sum_{\tau_{3i-1,T}}^{\tau_{3i,T}-1}\zeta(n)\Bigg]}_{\Pi_{3,T}}, \end{align} where \begin{align} C_{\Pi,0}&=g(\theta_{1})+6\Delta_{0}+5\alpha_{0}\sqrt{ L\Delta_{0}}+\frac{3 L\alpha_{0}^{2}}{2}, C_{\Pi,1}=\alpha_{0}\Big(\sqrt{\sigma_{0}}+\sqrt{\frac{\sigma_{1}}{\eta}}\Big)+\frac{ L\alpha_{0}^{2}}{2\sqrt{S_{0}}}\Big(\sigma_{0}+\frac{\sigma_{1}}{\eta}\Big). \end{align}

nodes.name: Equation (65)
nodes.statement: \mathbb{E}\Big[\sup_{1\le n<T}g(\theta_{n})\Big]\le C_{\Pi,0}+C_{\Pi, 1}\underbrace{\mathbb{E}\Bigg[\sum_{n=\tau_{1,T}}^{\tau_{3,T}-1}\zeta(n)+\sum_{i=2}^{+\infty}\sum_{\tau_{3i-1,T}}^{\tau_{3i,T}-1}\zeta(n)\Bigg]}_{\Pi_{3,T}},
nodes.label: wxm_200

nodes.name: Equation (66)
nodes.statement: C_{\Pi,0}&=g(\theta_{1})+6\Delta_{0}+5\alpha_{0}\sqrt{ L\Delta_{0}}+\frac{3 L\alpha_{0}^{2}}{2}, C_{\Pi,1}=\alpha_{0}\Big(\sqrt{\sigma_{0}}+\sqrt{\frac{\sigma_{1}}{\eta}}\Big)+\frac{ L\alpha_{0}^{2}}{2\sqrt{S_{0}}}\Big(\sigma_{0}+\frac{\sigma_{1}}{\eta}\Big).
nodes.label: constant_Pi

nodes.name: Recall Lemma 3.1
nodes.statement: Next, we turn to find an upper bound for $\Pi_{3,T}$ which is independent of $T$. Recall the sufficient decrease inequality in \cref{sufficient:lem} \begin{align*} \hat{g}(\theta_{n+1})-\hat{g}(\theta_{n}) & \le -\frac{\alpha_{0}}{4}\zeta_{n}+C_{\Gamma,1}\cdot \Gamma_n +C_{\Gamma,2}\frac{\Gamma_{n}}{\sqrt{S_{n}}} + \alpha_0 \hat{X}_{n}. \end{align*}

nodes.name: First segment of Pi_3
nodes.statement: First, we estimate the first term of $\Pi_{3,T}$. Telescoping the above inequality over $n$ from the interval \(I_{1,\tau}:=[\tau_{1,T},\tau_{3,T}-1]\) gives \begin{align*} \frac{\alpha_{0}}{4}\sum_{n \in I_{1,\tau}}\zeta(n)&\le \hat{g}(\theta_{\tau_{1,T}})-\hat{g}(\theta_{\tau_{3,T}})+C_{\Gamma,1}\sum_{n \in I_{1,\tau}} \Gamma_n+C_{\Gamma,2}\sum_{n \in I_{1,\tau}}\frac{\Gamma_{n}}{\sqrt{S_{n}}}+\alpha_0 \sum_{n \in I_{1,\tau}}\hat{X}_{n}. \end{align*} Taking the expectation on both sides of the above inequality, we have \begin{align*} \frac{\alpha_{0}}{4}\mathbb{E}\left[\sum_{n \in I_{1,\tau}}\zeta(n)\right]&\le\mathbb{E}\big[\hat{g}(\theta_{\tau_{1,T}})\big]+C_{\Gamma,1}\mathbb{E}\bigg[\sum_{n \in I_{1,\tau}} \Gamma_n \bigg]+C_{\Gamma,2}\mathbb{E}\Bigg[\sum_{n \in I_{1,\tau}}\frac{\Gamma_{n}}{\sqrt{S_{n}}}\Bigg]+\alpha_0\mathbb{E}\Bigg[\sum_{n \in I_{1,\tau}}\hat{X}_{n}\Bigg]\notag\\&\mathop{\le}^{(a)} \mathbb{E}\big[\hat{g}(\theta_{\tau_{1,T}})\big]+C_{\Gamma,1}\mathbb{E}\bigg[\sum_{n \in I_{1,\tau}} \mathbb{E}[\Gamma_n|\mathscr{F}_{n-1}]\bigg]+C_{\Gamma,2}\mathbb{E}\Bigg[\sum_{n \in I_{1,\tau}}\frac{\Gamma_{n}}{\sqrt{S_{n}}}\Bigg]+0, \end{align*} where for (a), we use \text{\emph{Doob's Stopped} theorem} (see \cref{vital1}) since the stopping times $\tau_{1,T}\le \tau_{3,T}-1$ and $\hat{X}_n$ is a martingale sequence. For the first term of the RHS of the above inequality, \begin{align*} \mathbb{E}\big[\hat{g}(\theta_{\tau_{1,T}})\big]&=\mathbb{E}\big[\mathbb{I}_{[\tau_{1}=1]}\hat{g}(\theta_{1})\big]+\mathbb{E}\big[\mathbb{I}_{\tau_{1}>1}\hat{g}(\theta_{\tau_{1,T}})\big] \\&\le \hat{g}(\theta_{1})+ \mathbb{E}\big[\mathbb{I}_{\tau_{1}>1}\hat{g}(\theta_{\tau_{1,T}-1})\big]+\mathbb{E}\big[\mathbb{I}_{\tau_{1}>1}(\hat{g}(\theta_{\tau_{1,T}})-\hat{g}(\theta_{\tau_{1,T}-1}))\big]\\&\mathop{\le}^{\text{\cref{lem:adj:ghat}}} \hat{g}(\theta_{1})+\Delta_{0}+h(\Delta_{0})<\hat{g}(\theta_{1})+\frac{3\Delta_{0}}{2}. \end{align*} We thus conclude that \begin{align} \frac{\alpha_{0}}{4}\mathbb{E}\left[\sum_{n \in I_{\tau,1}}\zeta(n)\right]&\le\hat{g}(\theta_{1})+\frac{3\Delta_{0}}{2}+C_{\Gamma,1}\mathbb{E}\bigg[\sum_{n \in I_{\tau,i}} \mathbb{E}[\Gamma_n|\mathscr{F}_{n-1}] \bigg]+C_{\Gamma,2}\mathbb{E}\Bigg[\sum_{n \in I_{\tau,i}}\frac{\Gamma_{n}}{\sqrt{S_{n}}}\Bigg]. \end{align}

nodes.name: Equation (67)
nodes.statement: \frac{\alpha_{0}}{4}\mathbb{E}\left[\sum_{n \in I_{\tau,1}}\zeta(n)\right]&\le\hat{g}(\theta_{1})+\frac{3\Delta_{0}}{2}+C_{\Gamma,1}\mathbb{E}\bigg[\sum_{n \in I_{\tau,i}} \mathbb{E}[\Gamma_n|\mathscr{F}_{n-1}] \bigg]+C_{\Gamma,2}\mathbb{E}\Bigg[\sum_{n \in I_{\tau,i}}\frac{\Gamma_{n}}{\sqrt{S_{n}}}\Bigg].
nodes.label: inequ:stat:1'

nodes.name: Later segments of Pi_3
nodes.statement: For the second term of $\Pi_{3,T}$, we telescope the sufficient decrease inequality in \cref{sufficient:lem} over $n$ from the interval \( I_{i,\tau}^{'}:= [\tau_{3i-1,T}, \tau_{3i,T}-1 ]\ (\forall\ i\ge 2)\) \begin{align} \frac{\alpha_{0}}{4}\sum_{n \in I_{i,\tau}^{'}}\zeta(n)&\le \hat{g}(\theta_{\tau_{3i-1,T}})-\hat{g}(\theta_{\tau_{3i,T}})+C_{\Gamma,1}\sum_{n \in I_{i,\tau}^{'}} \Gamma_n+C_{\Gamma,2}\sum_{n \in I_{i,\tau}^{'}}\frac{\Gamma_{n}}{\sqrt{S_{n}}}+\alpha_0 \sum_{n \in I_{i,\tau}^{'}}\hat{X}_{n}. \end{align} Recalling the definition of the stopping time $\tau_t$, we know that \(\tau_{3i,T} \geq \tau_{3i-1,T}\) always holds. In particular, \(\tau_{3i,T} = \tau_{3i-1,T}\) implies that \(\tau_{3i,T}-1 < \tau_{3i-1,T}\). Since $\sum_{n=a}^b(\cdot) = 0$ for $b < a$, we have $\sum_{n=\tau_{3i-1,T}}^{\tau_{3i,T}-1}(\cdot) = 0 $ and $\hat{g}(\theta_{\tau_{3i,T}}) = \hat{g}(\theta_{\tau_{3i-1,T}})$, then LHS and RHS of \cref{inequ:stab:2} are both zero and \cref{inequ:stab:2} holds. Taking the expectation on both sides and noting the equation of \cref{sum:expect:ab} gives \begin{align} \frac{\alpha_{0}}{4}\mathbb{E}\left[\sum_{n \in I_{i,\tau}^{'}}\zeta(n)\right]&\le \mathbb{E}\big[\hat{g}(\theta_{\tau_{3i-1,T}})-\hat{g}(\theta_{\tau_{3i,T}})\big]+C_{\Gamma,1}\mathbb{E}\bigg[\sum_{n \in I_{i,\tau}^{'}} \mathbb{E}[\Gamma_n|\mathscr{F}_{n-1}] \bigg]\notag\\&+C_{\Gamma,2}\mathbb{E}\Bigg[\sum_{n \in I_{i,\tau}^{'}}\frac{\Gamma_{n}}{\sqrt{S_{n}}}\Bigg]+0. \end{align}

nodes.name: Equation (68)
nodes.statement: \frac{\alpha_{0}}{4}\sum_{n \in I_{i,\tau}^{'}}\zeta(n)&\le \hat{g}(\theta_{\tau_{3i-1,T}})-\hat{g}(\theta_{\tau_{3i,T}})+C_{\Gamma,1}\sum_{n \in I_{i,\tau}^{'}} \Gamma_n+C_{\Gamma,2}\sum_{n \in I_{i,\tau}^{'}}\frac{\Gamma_{n}}{\sqrt{S_{n}}}+\alpha_0 \sum_{n \in I_{i,\tau}^{'}}\hat{X}_{n}.
nodes.label: inequ:stab:2

nodes.name: Equation (69)
nodes.statement: \frac{\alpha_{0}}{4}\mathbb{E}\left[\sum_{n \in I_{i,\tau}^{'}}\zeta(n)\right]&\le \mathbb{E}\big[\hat{g}(\theta_{\tau_{3i-1,T}})-\hat{g}(\theta_{\tau_{3i,T}})\big]+C_{\Gamma,1}\mathbb{E}\bigg[\sum_{n \in I_{i,\tau}^{'}} \mathbb{E}[\Gamma_n|\mathscr{F}_{n-1}] \bigg]\notag\\&+C_{\Gamma,2}\mathbb{E}\Bigg[\sum_{n \in I_{i,\tau}^{'}}\frac{\Gamma_{n}}{\sqrt{S_{n}}}\Bigg]+0.
nodes.label: inequ:stat:1

nodes.name: Bound endpoint values
nodes.statement: If \(\tau_{3i-1, T} < \tau_{3i, T}\), for any $n \in I_{i,\tau}^{'} = [\tau_{3i-1,T}, \tau_{3i,T}-1]$, by applying \cref{lem:adj:ghat} we have \begin{align*} \hat{g}(\theta_{\tau_{3i-1, T}}) - \hat{g}(\theta_{\tau_{3i,T}})&<\hat{g}(\theta_{\tau_{3i-1,T}}) < \hat{g}(\theta_{\tau_{3i-1,T}-1})+h(\hat{g}(\theta_{\tau_{3i-1,T}-1})). \end{align*} Based on the properties of the stopping time \(\tau_{3i-1},\) we have $\hat{g}(\theta_{\tau_{3i-1,T}-1}) \leq 2\Delta_{0}.$ Based on the above inequality, we further estimate the first term of \cref{inequ:stat:1} and achieve that \begin{align} \frac{\alpha_{0}}{4}\mathbb{E}\Bigg[\sum_{n=I_{i,\tau}^{'}}\zeta(n)\Bigg]\notag&\le C_{\Delta_{0}}\mathbb{E}\big[\mathbb{I}_{\{\tau_{3i-1,T}<\tau_{3i,T} \}}\big]+C_{\Gamma,1}\mathbb{E}\bigg[\sum_{n=I_{i,\tau}^{'}} \mathbb{E}[\Gamma_n|\mathscr{F}_{n-1}] \bigg] \\&+C_{\Gamma,2}\mathbb{E}\Bigg[\sum_{n=I_{i,\tau}^{'}}\frac{\Gamma_{n}}{\sqrt{S_{n}}}\Bigg] , \end{align} where \begin{align} C_{\Delta_{0}}: =2\Delta_{0}+ \sqrt{2 L}\left(1 + \frac{\sigma_0 L}{2\sqrt{S_0}}\right)\alpha_0\sqrt{2\Delta_0} + \left(1 + \frac{\sigma_0\alpha_0 L}{2\sqrt{S_0}}\right)\frac{ L\alpha_0^2}{2}. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Bound $\hat g$ drop by $C_{\Delta_0}$ via Lemma 3.2

nodes.name: Equation (70)
nodes.statement: \frac{\alpha_{0}}{4}\mathbb{E}\Bigg[\sum_{n=I_{i,\tau}^{'}}\zeta(n)\Bigg]\notag&\le C_{\Delta_{0}}\mathbb{E}\big[\mathbb{I}_{\{\tau_{3i-1,T}<\tau_{3i,T} \}}\big]+C_{\Gamma,1}\mathbb{E}\bigg[\sum_{n=I_{i,\tau}^{'}} \mathbb{E}[\Gamma_n|\mathscr{F}_{n-1}] \bigg] \\&+C_{\Gamma,2}\mathbb{E}\Bigg[\sum_{n=I_{i,\tau}^{'}}\frac{\Gamma_{n}}{\sqrt{S_{n}}}\Bigg] ,
nodes.label: wxm_90

nodes.name: Equation (71)
nodes.statement: C_{\Delta_{0}}: =2\Delta_{0}+ \sqrt{2 L}\left(1 + \frac{\sigma_0 L}{2\sqrt{S_0}}\right)\alpha_0\sqrt{2\Delta_0} + \left(1 + \frac{\sigma_0\alpha_0 L}{2\sqrt{S_0}}\right)\frac{ L\alpha_0^2}{2}.
nodes.label: inequ:C:Delta0

nodes.name: Sum over i
nodes.statement: Telescoping \cref{wxm_90} over $i$ from \(2\) to \(+\infty\) to estimate the second part of $\Pi_{3,T}$, we have \begin{align} \frac{\alpha_{0}}{4}\mathbb{E}\left[\sum_{i=2}^{+\infty}\sum_{n=I_{i,\tau}^{'}}\zeta(n)\right]\le& C_{\Delta_{0}}\cdot\sum_{i=2}^{+\infty}\mathbb{E}\big[\mathbb{I}_{\tau_{3i-1,T}<\tau_{3i,T}}\big]+C_{\Gamma,1}\sum_{i=2}^{+\infty}\mathbb{E}\bigg[\sum_{n=I_{i,\tau}^{'}} \mathbb{E}[\Gamma_n|\mathscr{F}_{n-1}]\bigg] \notag \\&+C_{\Gamma,2}\sum_{i=2}^{+\infty}\mathbb{E}\Bigg[\sum_{n=I_{i,\tau}^{'}}\frac{\Gamma_{n}}{\sqrt{S_{n}}}\Bigg]. \end{align}

nodes.name: Equation (72)
nodes.statement: \frac{\alpha_{0}}{4}\mathbb{E}\left[\sum_{i=2}^{+\infty}\sum_{n=I_{i,\tau}^{'}}\zeta(n)\right]\le& C_{\Delta_{0}}\cdot\sum_{i=2}^{+\infty}\mathbb{E}\big[\mathbb{I}_{\tau_{3i-1,T}<\tau_{3i,T}}\big]+C_{\Gamma,1}\sum_{i=2}^{+\infty}\mathbb{E}\bigg[\sum_{n=I_{i,\tau}^{'}} \mathbb{E}[\Gamma_n|\mathscr{F}_{n-1}]\bigg] \notag \\&+C_{\Gamma,2}\sum_{i=2}^{+\infty}\mathbb{E}\Bigg[\sum_{n=I_{i,\tau}^{'}}\frac{\Gamma_{n}}{\sqrt{S_{n}}}\Bigg].
nodes.label: pqwe_1

nodes.name: Conclude
nodes.statement: Note that the stopping time \(\tau_{t}\) is truncated for any finite time \(T\). For a specific $T$, the sum \(\sum_{i=2}^{+\infty}\) has only finite non-zero terms, thus we can interchange the order of summation and expectation \(\mathbb{E}\left(\sum_{i=2}^{+\infty} (\cdot) \right) = \sum_{i=2}^{+\infty} \left(\mathbb{E}(\cdot) \right).\) Substituting \cref{pqwe_1} and \cref{inequ:stat:1'} into \cref{wxm_200} gives \begin{align} &\mathbb{E}\Big[\sup_{1\le n< T}g(\theta_{n})\Big]\notag \\ \le&\ \overline{C}_{\Pi,0}+ C_{\Pi,1}C_{\Delta_{0}}\cdot\sum_{i=2}^{+\infty}\underbrace{\mathbb{E}\big[\mathbb{I}_{\tau_{3i-1,T}<\tau_{3i,T}}\big]}_{\Psi_{i,1}}+C_{\Pi,1}C_{\Gamma,1}\underbrace{\mathbb{E}\left[\bigg(\sum_{I_{1,\tau}}+\sum_{i=2}^{+\infty}\sum_{n=I_{i,\tau}^{'}} \bigg)\mathbb{E}[\Gamma_n|\mathscr{F}_{n-1}]\right]}_{\Psi_{2}} \notag \\&\quad +C_{\Pi,1}C_{\Gamma,2}\underbrace{\mathbb{E}\Bigg[\bigg(\sum_{n=I_{1,\tau}}+\sum_{i=2}^{+\infty}\sum_{n=I_{i,\tau}^{'}} \bigg)\frac{\Gamma_{n}}{\sqrt{S_{n}}}\Bigg]}_{\Psi_{3}}, \end{align} where $\overline{C}_{\Pi,0}:=\hat{g}(\theta_{1})+\frac{3\Delta_{0}}{2}+C_{\Pi,0}.$

nodes.name: Equation (73)
nodes.statement: &\mathbb{E}\Big[\sup_{1\le n< T}g(\theta_{n})\Big]\notag \\ \le&\ \overline{C}_{\Pi,0}+ C_{\Pi,1}C_{\Delta_{0}}\cdot\sum_{i=2}^{+\infty}\underbrace{\mathbb{E}\big[\mathbb{I}_{\tau_{3i-1,T}<\tau_{3i,T}}\big]}_{\Psi_{i,1}}+C_{\Pi,1}C_{\Gamma,1}\underbrace{\mathbb{E}\left[\bigg(\sum_{I_{1,\tau}}+\sum_{i=2}^{+\infty}\sum_{n=I_{i,\tau}^{'}} \bigg)\mathbb{E}[\Gamma_n|\mathscr{F}_{n-1}]\right]}_{\Psi_{2}} \notag \\&\quad +C_{\Pi,1}C_{\Gamma,2}\underbrace{\mathbb{E}\Bigg[\bigg(\sum_{n=I_{1,\tau}}+\sum_{i=2}^{+\infty}\sum_{n=I_{i,\tau}^{'}} \bigg)\frac{\Gamma_{n}}{\sqrt{S_{n}}}\Bigg]}_{\Psi_{3}},
nodes.label: wxm_110

nodes.name: Recall Lemma 3.1
nodes.statement: Due to \cref{sufficient:lem}, we know \begin{align} \hat{g}(\theta_{n+1})-\hat{g}(\theta_{n}) & \le -\frac{\alpha_{0}}{4}\zeta(n)+C_{\Gamma, 1}\cdot \Gamma_n + C_{\Gamma, 2}\frac{\Gamma_{n}}{\sqrt{S_{n}}} + \alpha_0 \hat{X}_{n}, \end{align}

nodes.name: Equation (74)
nodes.statement: \hat{g}(\theta_{n+1})-\hat{g}(\theta_{n}) & \le -\frac{\alpha_{0}}{4}\zeta(n)+C_{\Gamma, 1}\cdot \Gamma_n + C_{\Gamma, 2}\frac{\Gamma_{n}}{\sqrt{S_{n}}} + \alpha_0 \hat{X}_{n},
nodes.label: jh_20

nodes.name: Weight by y_n
nodes.statement: Then we define an auxiliary variable $ y_{n} := \frac{1}{\sqrt{S_{n-1}}}$. Multiplying both sides of \cref{jh_20} by this auxiliary variable, we obtain \begin{align*} y_{n}\hat{g}(\theta_{n+1})-y_{n}\hat{g}(\theta_{n}) & \le -\frac{\alpha_{0}}{4}y_{n}\zeta(n)+C_{\Gamma, 1}\cdot y_{n}\Gamma_n + C_{\Gamma, 2}y_{n}\frac{\Gamma_{n}}{\sqrt{S_{n}}} + \alpha_0 y_{n}\hat{X}_{n}\notag. \end{align*}

nodes.name: Rearrange
nodes.statement: By transposing the above inequality, and note that \(y_{n}g(\theta_{n+1}) - y_{n}g(\theta_{n}) = y_{n+1}g(\theta_{n+1}) - y_{n}g(\theta_{n}) + (y_{n} - y_{n+1})g(\theta_{n+1}),\) we obtain \begin{equation}\nonumber\begin{aligned} \frac{\alpha_{0}}{4}y_{n}\zeta(n)&\le \big(y_{n}\hat{g}(\theta_{n})-y_{n+1}\hat{g}(\theta_{n+1})\big)+{(y_{n+1}-y_{n})\hat{g}(\theta_{n+1})}+C_{\Gamma, 1}\cdot y_{n}\Gamma_n\\&+C_{\Gamma,2}y_{n}\frac{\Gamma_{n}}{\sqrt{S_{n}}}+\alpha_0 y_{n}\hat{X}_{n}. \end{aligned}\end{equation}

nodes.name: Telescope
nodes.statement: For any positive number \(T \ge 0\), we telescope the terms indexed by \(n\) from 1 to \(T\), and take the mathematical expectation, yielding \begin{align} \frac{\alpha_{0}}{4}\mathbb{E}\Bigg[\sum_{n=1}^{T}y_{n}\zeta_{n}\Bigg]&{\leq} y_{1}\hat{g}(\theta_{1})+\mathbb{E}\Bigg[\underbrace{\sum_{n=1}^{T}(y_{n+1}-y_{n})\hat{g}(\theta_{n+1})}_{\Theta_{1}}\Bigg]+C_{\Gamma,1}\cdot\underbrace{\sum_{n=1}^{T}y_{n}\Gamma_{n}}_{\Theta_{2}}+C_{\Gamma,2}\cdot\underbrace{\sum_{n=1}^{T}y_{n}\frac{\Gamma_{n}}{\sqrt{S_{n}}}}_{\Theta_{3}}+0. \end{align}

nodes.name: Equation (75)
nodes.statement: \frac{\alpha_{0}}{4}\mathbb{E}\Bigg[\sum_{n=1}^{T}y_{n}\zeta_{n}\Bigg]&{\leq} y_{1}\hat{g}(\theta_{1})+\mathbb{E}\Bigg[\underbrace{\sum_{n=1}^{T}(y_{n+1}-y_{n})\hat{g}(\theta_{n+1})}_{\Theta_{1}}\Bigg]+C_{\Gamma,1}\cdot\underbrace{\sum_{n=1}^{T}y_{n}\Gamma_{n}}_{\Theta_{2}}+C_{\Gamma,2}\cdot\underbrace{\sum_{n=1}^{T}y_{n}\frac{\Gamma_{n}}{\sqrt{S_{n}}}}_{\Theta_{3}}+0.
nodes.label: ada_q_1

nodes.name: Theta_1
nodes.statement: Our objective is to prove that the RHS of the above inequality has an upper bound independent of $T.$ To this end, we bound $\Theta_{1}$, $\Theta_{2}$, and $\Theta_{3}$ separately. For $\Theta_{2}$, we have \begin{align} \Theta_{1}&=\sum_{n=1}^{T}(y_{n+1}-y_{n})\hat{g}(\theta_{n+1})=\sum_{n=1}^{T}\Big(\frac{1}{\sqrt{S_{n+1}}}-\frac{1}{\sqrt{S_{n}}}\Big)\hat{g}(\theta_{n+1})\le 0. \end{align}

nodes.name: Equation (76)
nodes.statement: \Theta_{1}&=\sum_{n=1}^{T}(y_{n+1}-y_{n})\hat{g}(\theta_{n+1})=\sum_{n=1}^{T}\Big(\frac{1}{\sqrt{S_{n+1}}}-\frac{1}{\sqrt{S_{n}}}\Big)\hat{g}(\theta_{n+1})\le 0.
nodes.label: jh_02

nodes.name: Theta_2
nodes.statement: Then for term $\Theta_{2}$ in \cref{jh_02}, we have \begin{align} \Theta_{2}=\sum_{n=1}^{T}y_{n}\Gamma_{n}&\le \sum_{n=1}^{T}\frac{\Gamma_{n}}{\sqrt{S_{n-1}}}=\sum_{n=1}^{T}y_{n}\Gamma_{n}\le \sum_{n=1}^{T}\frac{\Gamma_{n}}{\sqrt{S_{n}}}+\sum_{n=1}^{T}\Gamma_{n}\bigg(\frac{1}{\sqrt{S_{n-1}}}-\frac{1}{\sqrt{S_{n}}}\bigg)\notag\\&\mathop{\le}^{(a)} \int_{S_{0}}^{+\infty}\frac{1}{x^{\frac{3}{2}}}\text{d}x+\frac{1}{\sqrt{S_{0}}}=\frac{3}{\sqrt{S_{0}}}. \end{align} In step $(a)$, we apply the series-integral inequality and the fact that \(\|\nabla g(\theta_{n})\|/\sqrt{S_{n}}\le 1.\)

nodes.name: Equation (77)
nodes.statement: \Theta_{2}=\sum_{n=1}^{T}y_{n}\Gamma_{n}&\le \sum_{n=1}^{T}\frac{\Gamma_{n}}{\sqrt{S_{n-1}}}=\sum_{n=1}^{T}y_{n}\Gamma_{n}\le \sum_{n=1}^{T}\frac{\Gamma_{n}}{\sqrt{S_{n}}}+\sum_{n=1}^{T}\Gamma_{n}\bigg(\frac{1}{\sqrt{S_{n-1}}}-\frac{1}{\sqrt{S_{n}}}\bigg)\notag\\&\mathop{\le}^{(a)} \int_{S_{0}}^{+\infty}\frac{1}{x^{\frac{3}{2}}}\text{d}x+\frac{1}{\sqrt{S_{0}}}=\frac{3}{\sqrt{S_{0}}}.
nodes.label: jh_03

nodes.name: Theta_3
nodes.statement: Finally for term \(\Theta_{3}\), we only need to use the series-integral inequality to get \begin{align} \Theta_{3}=\sum_{n=1}^{T}y_{n}\frac{\Gamma_{n}}{\sqrt{S_{n}}}\le \frac{1}{\sqrt{S_{0}}}\int_{S_{0}}^{+\infty}\le \frac{2}{S_{0}}. \end{align}

nodes.name: Equation (78)
nodes.statement: \Theta_{3}=\sum_{n=1}^{T}y_{n}\frac{\Gamma_{n}}{\sqrt{S_{n}}}\le \frac{1}{\sqrt{S_{0}}}\int_{S_{0}}^{+\infty}\le \frac{2}{S_{0}}.
nodes.label: jh_04

nodes.name: Combine
nodes.statement: Subsequently, we substitute the estimates for $\Theta_{1}$, $\Theta_{2},$ and $\Theta_{3}$ from \cref{jh_02}, \cref{jh_03}, and \cref{jh_04} back into \cref{ada_q_1}, resulting in the following inequality \begin{align*} \frac{\alpha_{0}}{4}\mathbb{E}\Bigg[\sum_{n=1}^{T}y_{n}\zeta_{n}\Bigg]&{\leq} y_{1}\hat{g}(\theta_{1})+0+\frac{3C_{\Gamma,1}}{\sqrt{S_{0}}}+\frac{2C_{\Gamma,2}}{S_{0}}<+\infty. \end{align*}

nodes.name: Monotone convergence
nodes.statement: The right-hand side of the above inequality is independent of \(T\). Therefore, by applying the \emph{ Lebesgue's monotone convergence} theorem, we obtain \begin{align*} \frac{\alpha_{0}}{4}\mathbb{E}\Bigg[\sum_{n=1}^{+\infty}y_{n}\zeta_{n}\Bigg]&{\leq} y_{1}\hat{g}(\theta_{1})+\frac{3C_{\Gamma,1}}{\sqrt{S_{0}}}+\frac{2C_{\Gamma,2}}{S_{0}}<+\infty. \end{align*} Then, \begin{align*} \mathbb{E}\Bigg[\sum_{n=1}^{+\infty}\frac{\|\nabla g(\theta_{n})\|^{2}}{S_{n-1}}\Bigg]\le M:=\hat{g}(\theta_{1})+\frac{3C_{\Gamma,1}}{\sqrt{S_{0}}}+\frac{2C_{\Gamma,2}}{S_{0}}<+\infty, \end{align*} where $M$ is a constant.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 3.6
nodes.statement: (of \cref{lem:psi:i1}) We start by observing the inequality \[\Psi_{i,1}=\mathbb{E}[\mathbb{I}_{\tau_{3i-1, T} < \tau_{3i, T}}]=\mathbb{P}(\tau_{3i-1, T} < \tau_{3i, T}).\] What we need to consider is the probability of the event $\tau_{3i-1, T} < \tau_{3i, T}$ occurring. In the case we consider $\tau_{3i-1, T} < \tau_{3i, T}$ which implies that $\hat{g}(\theta_{3i-1, T}) \geq 2\Delta_0$. On the other hand, according to the definition of the stopping time $\tau_{3i-2,T}$, we have $\hat{g}(\tau_{{3i-2, T}-1}) \leq \Delta_0$. Then \begin{align*} \hat{g}(\theta_{\tau_{3i-2,T}}) < \hat{g}(\theta_{\tau_{3i-2,T}-1})+h(\hat{g}(\theta_{\tau_{3i-2,T}-1})) \leq \Delta_0 + h(\Delta_0) < \frac{3}{2}\Delta_0. \end{align*} Since \(\Delta_0 > C_{0}\), we know that \( h(\Delta_0) < \frac{1}{2}\Delta_0\) by \cref{lem:adj:ghat}. Then, by \cref{sufficient:lem}), \begin{align*} \frac{\Delta_0}{2} &=2\Delta_0-\frac{3\Delta_0}{2}\le \hat{g}(\theta_{\tau_{3i-1,T}})-\hat{g}(\theta_{\tau_{3i-2,T}})\le \sum_{n=\tau_{3i-2,T}}^{\tau_{3i-1,T}-1}(\hat{g}(\theta_{n+1})-\hat{g}(\theta_{n}))\\&\le C_{\Gamma,1}\cdot \sum_{n=\tau_{3i-2,T}}^{\tau_{3i-1,T}-1}\Gamma_n +C_{\Gamma,2}\sum_{n=\tau_{3i-2,T}}^{\tau_{3i-1,T}-1}\frac{\Gamma_{n}}{\sqrt{S_{n}}} + \alpha_0\Bigg| \sum_{n=\tau_{3i-2,T}}^{\tau_{3i-1,T}-1}\hat{X}_{n}\Bigg|\\& \mathop{\le}^{\text{Young's inequality}} C_{\Gamma,1}\cdot \sum_{n=\tau_{3i-2,T}}^{\tau_{3i-1,T}-1}\Gamma_n +C_{\Gamma,2}\sum_{n=\tau_{3i-2,T}}^{\tau_{3i-1,T}-1}\frac{\Gamma_{n}}{\sqrt{S_{n}}}+\frac{\alpha_0^{2}}{\Delta_0}\Bigg( \sum_{n=\tau_{3i-2,T}}^{\tau_{3i-1,T}-1}\hat{X}_{n}\Bigg)^{2} + \frac{\Delta_0}{4}, \end{align*} which further induces that \begin{equation}\begin{aligned} \frac{\Delta_0}{4}&\le C_{\Gamma,1}\cdot \sum_{n=\tau_{3i-2,T}}^{\tau_{3i-1,T}-1}\Gamma_n +C_{\Gamma,2}\sum_{n=\tau_{3i-2,T}}^{\tau_{3i-1,T}-1}\frac{\Gamma_{n}}{\sqrt{S_{n}}} + \frac{\alpha_0^{2}}{\Delta_0}\Bigg( \sum_{n=\tau_{3i-2,T}}^{\tau_{3i-1,T}-1}\hat{X}_{n}\Bigg)^{2}. \end{aligned}\end{equation} Based on the above analysis, we can obtain the following sequence of event inclusions \begin{align*} \{\tau_{3i-1,T}<\tau_{3i,T}\}&\subset \{\hat{g}(\theta_{3i-1,T})>2\Delta_{0}\}\subset\Big\{\frac{\Delta_{0}}{2}\le \hat{g}(\theta_{\tau_{3i-1,T}})-\hat{g}(\theta_{\tau_{3i-2,T}})\Big\}\\&\subset\{\text{\cref{power_00} holds}\}. \end{align*} Thus, we have the following probability inequality \begin{align*} \mathbb{E}[\mathbb{I}_{\tau_{3i-1,T}<\tau_{3i,T}}]=\mathbb{P}(\tau_{3i-1,T}<\tau_{3i,T})\le \mathbb{P}(\text{\cref{power_00} holds}). \end{align*} Then, according to \emph{Markov's inequality}, we obtain \begin{align*} \mathbb{P}(\text{\cref{power_00} holds})&\le \frac{4}{\Delta_0}C_{\Gamma,1}\cdot \mathbb{E}\Bigg[\sum_{n=\tau_{3i-2,T}}^{\tau_{3i-1,T}-1}\Gamma_n\Bigg] \\&+ \frac{4C_{\Gamma,2}}{\Delta_0}\mathbb{E}\Bigg[\sum_{n=\tau_{3i-2,T}}^{\tau_{3i-1,T}-1}\frac{\Gamma_{n}}{\sqrt{S_{n}}}\Bigg] + \frac{4\alpha_0^{2}}{\Delta_0^{2}}\mathbb{E}\Bigg[\sum_{n=\tau_{3i-2,T}}^{\tau_{3i-1,T}-1}\hat{X}_{n}\Bigg]^{2}\\&\mathop{=}^{\text{\cref{sum:expect:ab}}} \frac{4C_{\Gamma,1}}{\Delta_0}\cdot \mathbb{E}\Bigg[\sum_{n=\tau_{3i-2,T}}^{\tau_{3i-1,T}-1}\mathbb{E}[\Gamma_n|\mathscr{F}_{n-1}]\Bigg] + \frac{4C_{\Gamma,2}}{\Delta_0}\mathbb{E}\Bigg[\sum_{n=\tau_{3i-2,T}}^{\tau_{3i-1,T}-1}\frac{\Gamma_{n}}{\sqrt{S_{n}}}\Bigg]\\& + \frac{4\alpha_0^{2}}{\Delta_0^{2}}\mathbb{E}\Bigg[\sum_{n=\tau_{3i-2,T}}^{\tau_{3i-1,T}-1}\hat{X}_{n}^{2}\bigg]. \end{align*} This completes the proof.
nodes.statement_short: An upcrossing of $\hat g$ from below $\tfrac32\Delta_0$ to $2\Delta_0$ forces a large accumulated increment; Markov's inequality bounds its probability.

nodes.statement: We start by observing the inequality \[\Psi_{i,1}=\mathbb{E}[\mathbb{I}_{\tau_{3i-1, T} < \tau_{3i, T}}]=\mathbb{P}(\tau_{3i-1, T} < \tau_{3i, T}).\]

nodes.name: Start value bound
nodes.statement: What we need to consider is the probability of the event $\tau_{3i-1, T} < \tau_{3i, T}$ occurring. In the case we consider $\tau_{3i-1, T} < \tau_{3i, T}$ which implies that $\hat{g}(\theta_{3i-1, T}) \geq 2\Delta_0$. On the other hand, according to the definition of the stopping time $\tau_{3i-2,T}$, we have $\hat{g}(\tau_{{3i-2, T}-1}) \leq \Delta_0$. Then \begin{align*} \hat{g}(\theta_{\tau_{3i-2,T}}) < \hat{g}(\theta_{\tau_{3i-2,T}-1})+h(\hat{g}(\theta_{\tau_{3i-2,T}-1})) \leq \Delta_0 + h(\Delta_0) < \frac{3}{2}\Delta_0. \end{align*}

nodes.name: Increment lower bound
nodes.statement: Since \(\Delta_0 > C_{0}\), we know that \( h(\Delta_0) < \frac{1}{2}\Delta_0\) by \cref{lem:adj:ghat}. Then, by \cref{sufficient:lem}), \begin{align*} \frac{\Delta_0}{2} &=2\Delta_0-\frac{3\Delta_0}{2}\le \hat{g}(\theta_{\tau_{3i-1,T}})-\hat{g}(\theta_{\tau_{3i-2,T}})\le \sum_{n=\tau_{3i-2,T}}^{\tau_{3i-1,T}-1}(\hat{g}(\theta_{n+1})-\hat{g}(\theta_{n}))\\&\le C_{\Gamma,1}\cdot \sum_{n=\tau_{3i-2,T}}^{\tau_{3i-1,T}-1}\Gamma_n +C_{\Gamma,2}\sum_{n=\tau_{3i-2,T}}^{\tau_{3i-1,T}-1}\frac{\Gamma_{n}}{\sqrt{S_{n}}} + \alpha_0\Bigg| \sum_{n=\tau_{3i-2,T}}^{\tau_{3i-1,T}-1}\hat{X}_{n}\Bigg|\\& \mathop{\le}^{\text{Young's inequality}} C_{\Gamma,1}\cdot \sum_{n=\tau_{3i-2,T}}^{\tau_{3i-1,T}-1}\Gamma_n +C_{\Gamma,2}\sum_{n=\tau_{3i-2,T}}^{\tau_{3i-1,T}-1}\frac{\Gamma_{n}}{\sqrt{S_{n}}}+\frac{\alpha_0^{2}}{\Delta_0}\Bigg( \sum_{n=\tau_{3i-2,T}}^{\tau_{3i-1,T}-1}\hat{X}_{n}\Bigg)^{2} + \frac{\Delta_0}{4}, \end{align*} which further induces that \begin{equation} \begin{aligned} \frac{\Delta_0}{4}&\le C_{\Gamma,1}\cdot \sum_{n=\tau_{3i-2,T}}^{\tau_{3i-1,T}-1}\Gamma_n +C_{\Gamma,2}\sum_{n=\tau_{3i-2,T}}^{\tau_{3i-1,T}-1}\frac{\Gamma_{n}}{\sqrt{S_{n}}} + \frac{\alpha_0^{2}}{\Delta_0}\Bigg( \sum_{n=\tau_{3i-2,T}}^{\tau_{3i-1,T}-1}\hat{X}_{n}\Bigg)^{2}. \end{aligned}\end{equation}

nodes.name: Equation (80)
nodes.statement: \begin{aligned} \frac{\Delta_0}{4}&\le C_{\Gamma,1}\cdot \sum_{n=\tau_{3i-2,T}}^{\tau_{3i-1,T}-1}\Gamma_n +C_{\Gamma,2}\sum_{n=\tau_{3i-2,T}}^{\tau_{3i-1,T}-1}\frac{\Gamma_{n}}{\sqrt{S_{n}}} + \frac{\alpha_0^{2}}{\Delta_0}\Bigg( \sum_{n=\tau_{3i-2,T}}^{\tau_{3i-1,T}-1}\hat{X}_{n}\Bigg)^{2}. \end{aligned}
nodes.label: power_00

nodes.name: Event inclusion
nodes.statement: Based on the above analysis, we can obtain the following sequence of event inclusions \begin{align*} \{\tau_{3i-1,T}<\tau_{3i,T}\}&\subset \{\hat{g}(\theta_{3i-1,T})>2\Delta_{0}\}\subset\Big\{\frac{\Delta_{0}}{2}\le \hat{g}(\theta_{\tau_{3i-1,T}})-\hat{g}(\theta_{\tau_{3i-2,T}})\Big\}\\&\subset\{\text{\cref{power_00} holds}\}. \end{align*} Thus, we have the following probability inequality \begin{align*} \mathbb{E}[\mathbb{I}_{\tau_{3i-1,T}<\tau_{3i,T}}]=\mathbb{P}(\tau_{3i-1,T}<\tau_{3i,T})\le \mathbb{P}(\text{\cref{power_00} holds}). \end{align*}

nodes.name: Markov
nodes.statement: Then, according to \emph{Markov's inequality}, we obtain \begin{align*} \mathbb{P}(\text{\cref{power_00} holds})&\le \frac{4}{\Delta_0}C_{\Gamma,1}\cdot \mathbb{E}\Bigg[\sum_{n=\tau_{3i-2,T}}^{\tau_{3i-1,T}-1}\Gamma_n\Bigg] \\&+ \frac{4C_{\Gamma,2}}{\Delta_0}\mathbb{E}\Bigg[\sum_{n=\tau_{3i-2,T}}^{\tau_{3i-1,T}-1}\frac{\Gamma_{n}}{\sqrt{S_{n}}}\Bigg] + \frac{4\alpha_0^{2}}{\Delta_0^{2}}\mathbb{E}\Bigg[\sum_{n=\tau_{3i-2,T}}^{\tau_{3i-1,T}-1}\hat{X}_{n}\Bigg]^{2}\\&\mathop{=}^{\text{\cref{sum:expect:ab}}} \frac{4C_{\Gamma,1}}{\Delta_0}\cdot \mathbb{E}\Bigg[\sum_{n=\tau_{3i-2,T}}^{\tau_{3i-1,T}-1}\mathbb{E}[\Gamma_n|\mathscr{F}_{n-1}]\Bigg] + \frac{4C_{\Gamma,2}}{\Delta_0}\mathbb{E}\Bigg[\sum_{n=\tau_{3i-2,T}}^{\tau_{3i-1,T}-1}\frac{\Gamma_{n}}{\sqrt{S_{n}}}\Bigg]\\& + \frac{4\alpha_0^{2}}{\Delta_0^{2}}\mathbb{E}\Bigg[\sum_{n=\tau_{3i-2,T}}^{\tau_{3i-1,T}-1}\hat{X}_{n}^{2}\bigg]. \end{align*} This completes the proof.

abla g(	heta_{n+1};\xi_{n+1})\|^{2}  ig| \mathscr{F}_{n} ig] \leq \sigma_0\|
abla g(	heta_{n+1})\|^{2} + \sigma_{1}\), it induces that  egin{align} \sum_{n=1}^{+\infty} rac{\|

Therefore, combining the above estimations for $\Xi_1, \Xi_2, \Xi_3$, we prove that the following relation holds on the event $\mathcal{S}$: \[\sum_{n=1}^{+\infty} rac{\|

nodes.statement: Firstly, when $\lim_{n\rightarrow+\infty}S_{n} < +\infty,$ we clearly have \[\sum_{n=1}^{+\infty}\frac{1}{\sqrt{S_{n}}} = +\infty.\]

nodes.statement: Next, for any stopping time $\tau$ that satisfies $[\tau=i] \in \mathscr{F}_{i-1}\ (\forall\ i>0)$, telescoping the index $n$ from $1$ to $\tau\wedge T-1$ in \cref{inequ:sufficient:key} and taking expectation on the above inequality yields \begin{equation} \begin{aligned} &\mathbb{E}\big[{g^{2}(\theta_{\tau\wedge T})}\big]-\mathbb{E}\big[{g^{2}(\theta_{1})}\big]\le- \alpha_0 \mathbb{E}\bigg[\sum_{n=1}^{\tau\wedge T-1}g(\theta_{n}) \zeta(n)\bigg]\\&+4 L\alpha_{0}\sigma_{0}\mathbb{E}\bigg[\sum_{n=1}^{\tau\wedge T-1}g^{2}(\theta_{n})\mathbb{E}\bigg[\Delta_{S,n}\bigg|\mathscr{F}_{n-1}\bigg]\bigg]+4\alpha_{0}\sigma_{1}\mathbb{E}\bigg[\sum_{n=1}^{\tau\wedge T-1}g(\theta_{n})\mathbb{E}\bigg[\Delta_{S,n}\bigg|\mathscr{F}_{n-1}\bigg]\bigg]\\&+\mathbb{E}\bigg[\sum_{n=1}^{\tau\wedge T-1}\left((2+2\alpha_0^2) Lg(\theta_n) + \frac{3\alpha_0^4 L^2}{4} \right) \Gamma_n\bigg]+2\alpha_0\mathbb{E}\bigg[\sum_{n=1}^{\tau\wedge T-1} \hat{Y}_n\bigg]. \end{aligned}\end{equation}

Substituting the above estimations into \cref{jrn_5} we have  egin{align} &\mathbb{E} ig({g^{2}(	heta_{	au\wedge T})} ig)-\mathbb{E} ig[{g^{2}(	heta_{1})} ig]\le-  rac{3\alpha_{0}}{4}\mathbb{E} igg[\sum_{n=1}^{	au\wedge T-1} g(	heta_{n}) \zeta(n) igg] + rac{\alpha_{0}}{4}\mathbb{E} igg[] \zeta(n) igg] + 	ilde{C}_1\mathbb{E} igg[\sum_{n=1}^{	au\wedge T-1} rac{g(	heta_{n})\Gamma_n}{\sqrt{S_{n}}} igg] 
otag \& +	ilde{C}_{2}\mathbb{E} igg[\sum_{n=1}^{	au\wedge T-1} g(	heta_{n}) \Gamma_n igg] +	ilde{C}_3\mathbb{E} igg[\sum_{n=1}^{	au\wedge T-1} rac{\Gamma_n}{\sqrt{S_{n}}} igg]+ rac{3\alpha_{0}^2 L^2}{4}\mathbb{E} igg[\sum_{n=1}^{	au\wedge T-1} \Gamma_n igg] + \mathcal{O}(1), \end{align} where  egin{align} 	ilde{C}_{1}&:=64\sigma_0^2\alpha_0^3 L^2 + 8\sigma_0\alpha_0(1+\alpha_0^2) L^2,\ \ 	ilde{C}_{2}:= 2(1+\alpha_0^2) L,

We notice the following facts  egin{align} &\sum_{n=1}^{	au\wedge T-1} \Gamma_n \leq \sum_{n=1}^{T}\Gamma_n = \sum_{n=1}^{T} rac{\|
abla g(	heta_{n},\xi_{n})\|^{2}}{S_{n}}<\int_{S_{0}}^{S_{T}} rac{1}{x}	ext{d}x<\ln S_{T}-\ln S_{0}, 
otag \& \sum_{n=1}^{	au\wedge T-1} rac{\Gamma_n}{\sqrt{S_n}}\le \sum_{n=1}^{+\infty} rac{\|

We then use these facts to simplify \cref{jrn_8} as  egin{align} &\quad\mathbb{E} ig[{g^{2}(	heta_{	au\wedge T})} ig] 
otag \ &\le-  rac{3\alpha_{0}}{4}\mathbb{E} igg[\sum_{n=1}^{	au\wedge T-1} g(	heta_{n}) \zeta(n) igg]+ 2\left( rac{\sigma_1}{\sqrt{S_0}} + \alpha_0 Light)\mathbb{E}[\ln S_{T}]+	ilde{C}_1\mathbb{E}\left[\sup_{n\le T}g(	heta_{n}) \sum_{n=1}^{	au\wedge T-1} rac{\Gamma_n}{\sqrt{S_n}}ight]
otag \ & \quad +	ilde{C}_2\mathbb{E}\left[ ig(\sup_{n\le T}g(	heta_{n}) ig) \cdot \sum_{n=1}^{	au\wedge T-1}\Gamma_night] +  rac{2	ilde{C}_3}{\sqrt{S_0}} + rac{3\alpha_{0}^2 L^2}{4}\mathbb{E}\left[\ln S_{T}ight] + \mathcal{O}(1)

otag \ &\quad +	ilde{C}_2\mathbb{E}\left[\sup_{n\le T}g(	heta_{n}) \cdot \ln(S_T)ight] +  rac{3\alpha_{0}^2 L^2}{4}\mathbb{E}\left[\ln S_{T}ight]+ \mathcal{O}(1). \end{align}

nodes.name: Equation (95)
nodes.statement:
&\quad\mathbb{E} ig[{g^{2}(	heta_{	au\wedge T})} ig] 
otag \ &\le-  rac{3\alpha_{0}}{4}\mathbb{E} igg[\sum_{n=1}^{	au\wedge T-1} g(	heta_{n}) \zeta(n) igg]+ 2\left( rac{\sigma_1}{\sqrt{S_0}} + \alpha_0 Light)\mathbb{E}[\ln S_{T}]+	ilde{C}_1\mathbb{E}\left[\sup_{n\le T}g(	heta_{n}) \sum_{n=1}^{	au\wedge T-1} rac{\Gamma_n}{\sqrt{S_n}}ight]

nodes.name: Tail bound
nodes.statement:
Then for any $\lambda>0,$ we define a stopping time $	au^{(\lambda)}:=\min\Big\{n:{g^{2}(	heta_{n})}>\lambda\Big\}.$ For any$\ \lambda_{0}>0,$ we let $	au = 	au^{(\ln T)\lambda_{0}}\wedge T\ ( orall\ T\ge 3)$ in \cref{inequ:lem:v2:1} and use the \emph{ Markov's inequality}  egin{align} \mathbb{P}\Bigg( rac{\sup_{1\le n\le T}{g^{ rac{3}{2}}(	heta_{n})}}{\ln^{ rac{3}{2}} T}>\lambda_{0}\Bigg)&=\mathbb{P}\Big(\sup_{1\le n\le T}{g^{2}(	heta_{n})}>\lambda^{ rac{4}{3}}_{0}\ln^{2} T\Big)=\mathbb{E}\left[\mathbb{I}_{	au^{(\ln^{2}T)\lambda_{0}}\wedge T}ight]
otag \ &\le  rac{1}{\lambda^{ rac{4}{3}}_{0}\ln^{2} T}\cdot\mathbb{E}\left[{g^{2}(	heta_{	au^{(\ln^{2} T)\lambda_{0}}\wedge T})}ight] 
otag \ &\mathop{\le}^{(a)} rac{\phi_{0}}{\lambda^{ rac{4}{3}}_{0} \ln T}\Bigg(\mathbb{E} igg[ rac{\sup_{1\le k\le n}{g^{ rac{3}{2}}(	heta_{n})}}{\ln^{ rac{3}{2}} T} igg]\Bigg)^{ rac{2}{3}}+ rac{\phi_{1}}{\lambda_{0}^{ rac{4}{3}}\ln^2 T},\end{align} where $\phi_0 = rac{2	ilde{C}_1}{\sqrt{S_0}} + \left(4\ln T + 2\sqrt{S_0} ight) + 2 \left(\mathbb{E}\ln^{3}(\zeta)ight)^{ rac{1}{3}}$ and $\phi_1 = 2\left( rac{\sigma_1}{\sqrt{S_0}} + \alpha_0 Light)\mathbb{E}\left[\ln S_{T}ight] + \mathcal{O}(1)$. The last inequality $(a)$ follows $\ln T>1\ ( orall\ T\ge 3)$, and since $g(x) = x^{3/2}$ is convex, by Jensen inequality  egin{align} \mathbb{E}\left[\sup_{n\le T}g(	heta_{n}) ight]^{ rac{3}{2}} & \leq \mathbb{E}\left[\sup_{n\le T}g^{ rac{3}{2}}(	heta_{n}) ight] 
otag \end{align} and by \emph{Holder inequality} and the upper bound of $S_T \leq \left(1+\zetaight)^2T^4$ and $\zeta = \sqrt{S_{0}}+\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\|
abla g(	heta_{n},\xi_{n})\|^{2}/n^2$ is uniformly bounded in \cref{lem_S_{T}}. We have  egin{align} \mathbb{E}\left[\sup_{n\le T}g(	heta_{n}) \cdot \ln(S_T)ight] & \leq 4\ln T\mathbb{E}\left[\sup_{n\le T}g(	heta_{n}) ight] + 2\mathbb{E}\left[\sup_{n\le T}g(	heta_{n})\ln( 1+\zeta) ight] 
otag \ & \mathop{\leq}^{(a)} \left(4\ln T + 2\sqrt{S_0} ight)\left(\mathbb{E}\sup_{n\le T}g^{ rac{3}{2}}(	heta_{n})ight)^{ rac{2}{3}} +2\mathbb{E}\left[\sup_{n\le T}g^{ rac{3}{2}}(	heta_{n})ight]^{ rac{2}{3}} \left(\mathbb{E}\ln^{3}(\zeta)ight)^{ rac{1}{3}}. \end{align} In step $(a)$, we first used the common inequality $\ln(1+x)\le x\ ( orall\ x>-1)$, and then applied the \emph{Hölder's} inequality, i.e., $\mathbb{E}[XY]\le \mathbb{E}^{ rac{2}{3}}[\|X\|^{ rac{3}{2}}]\mathbb{E}^{ rac{1}{3}}[\|Y\|^{3}].$

nodes.statement: The sequence \(\{\eta_t\}_{t\ge 1}\) is monotonically decreasing per coordinate with respect to \( t \).

Since \begin{align*} \eta_{t,i}=\frac{\alpha_t}{\sqrt{v_{t,i}}+\epsilon}=\frac{\sqrt{t}\alpha_t}{\sqrt{tv_{t,i}}+\sqrt{t}\epsilon}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{tv_{t,i}}+\sqrt{t}\epsilon}, \end{align*} where the global learning rate $\alpha_t = 1/\sqrt{t}$ and the denominator is monotonically non-increasing and greater than 0. The proofs of these lemmas are omitted, because they are straightforward and follow the same arguments as the corresponding lemmas, \cref{lem:adj:ghat} and \cref{pro_0}, for AdaGrad-Norm.  egin{lem} For the Lyapunov function $\hat{g}(	heta_n),$ there is a constant $C_0$ such that for any $\hat{g}(	heta_{n}) \geq C_0$, we have $$\hat{g}(	heta_{n+1})-\hat{g}(	heta_{n})\leq \hat{g}(	heta_{n})/2. $$ \end{lem}  egin{property} Under~\cref{coordinate_0,coordinate}, the gradient sublevel set $J_{\eta}:= igcup_{i=1}^{d}\{	heta \mid (

Then, by~\cref{coordinate_0,coordinate}, there exist a constant $\hat{C}_{g} > 0$ such that the function $\hat{g}(	heta) < \hat{C}_{g}$ for any $	heta \in J_{\eta}$. \end{property}  egin{proof}(of \cref{bound''}) First, we define \(\Delta_{0} := \max\{C_{0}, 2\hat{g}(	heta_{1}), \hat{C}_{g}\}\). nodes.name: One-step growth bound for the RMSProp Lyapunov function
nodes.statement: For the Lyapunov function $\hat{g}(\theta_n),$ there is a constant $C_0$ such that for any $\hat{g}(\theta_{n}) \geq C_0$, we have $$\hat{g}(\theta_{n+1})-\hat{g}(\theta_{n})\leq \hat{g}(\theta_{n})/2. $$

nodes.name: Lyapunov function bounded on coordinate-wise gradient sublevel sets
nodes.statement: Under~\cref{coordinate_0,coordinate}, the gradient sublevel set $J_{\eta}:=\bigcup_{i=1}^{d}\{\theta \mid (\nabla_{i} g(\theta))^{2}\le \eta\}$ with $\eta >0$ is a closed bounded set. Then, by~\cref{coordinate_0,coordinate}, there exist a constant $\hat{C}_{g} > 0$ such that the function $\hat{g}(\theta) < \hat{C}_{g}$ for any $\theta \in J_{\eta}$.

In fact, \begin{align*} \sum_{j=1}^{+\infty}A_{j,1}&\le \frac{1}{\epsilon}\left(\sigma_{0}+\frac{\sigma_{1}}{\eta}\right)\mathbb{E}\left[\sum_{j=1}^{+\infty}\sum_{t=\tau_{3j-2,T}}^{\tau_{3j-1,T}-1}\sum_{i=1}^{d}\frac{\eta_{{t-1},i}}{\sqrt{t}}(\nabla_{i}g(\theta_{t}))^{2}\right] \leq \mathcal{O}\left(\sum_{t=1}^{+\infty}\sum_{i=1}^{d}\frac{\eta_{{t-1},i}}{\sqrt{t}}(\nabla_{i}g(\theta_{t}))^{2}\right)\\&\mathop{\le}^{\text{\cref{RMSProp_0} with $\delta=1/2$}}\mathcal{O}(1). \end{align*}

nodes.name: Sum A_{j,2}
nodes.statement: Then, following the same procedure as $A_{j,1}$ to estimate \(A_{j,2}\), we obtain that \begin{align*} \sum_{j=1}^{+\infty}A_{j,2}\le \mathcal{O}\left(\sum_{t=1}^{+\infty}\sum_{i=1}^{d}\frac{\eta_{{t-1},i}}{\sqrt{t}}(\nabla_{i}g(\theta_{t}))^{2}\right)\mathop{\le}^{\text{\cref{RMSProp_0} with $\delta=1/2$}}\mathcal{O}(1). \end{align*}

nodes.statement: According to \cref{RMSprop_2}, combining the estimates for $A_{j,1}$ and $A_{j,2}$ gives \begin{align*} \sum_{j=1}^{+\infty}\mathbb{E}\left[\mathbb{I}_{\tau_{3j-1,T}<\tau_{3j,T}}\right]\le \mathcal{O}\left(\sum_{j=1}^{+\infty}A_{j,1}\right)+\mathcal{O}\left(\sum_{j=1}^{+\infty}A_{j,2}\right)\le \mathcal{O}(1). \end{align*}

nodes.name: Conclude
nodes.statement: Substituting the above estimate into \cref{RMSprop_6}, and then into \cref{RMSprop_5} and \cref{RMSprop_7}, we obtain \begin{align*} \mathbb{E}\left[\sup_{1\le n<T}\hat{g}(\theta_{n})\right] \le \mathcal{O}(1). \end{align*} where the constant hidden in \(\mathcal{O}\) is independent of \(T\). Taking \(T \to +\infty\) and applying the \emph{Lebesgue's Monotone Convergence} theorem, we have $\mathbb{E}\left[\sup_{n\ge 1}\hat{g}(\theta_{n})\right] \leq \mathcal{O}(1) $ which implies \[\mathbb{E}\left[\sup_{n\ge 1}{g}(\theta_{n})\right] \leq \mathcal{O}(1).\]
